jobs.company: School of American Ballet at Lincoln Center
jobs.title: Director of Institutional Giving
jobs.description:
**Organization Overview**


The School of American Ballet (SAB) at Lincoln Center, founded by George Balanchine and Lincoln Kirstein, is the preeminent ballet school in the country. Our mission is to train professional dancers for careers in classical ballet. We provide the resources for a diverse pool of students to train at the highest level – with 15\-25 a year going on to dance for New York City Ballet, our official but independent ballet company, and other major ballet companies worldwide. SAB has a far\-reaching impact on the art form and enriches the lives of each student who comes through its doors, over 800 annually, ages 6 to 18\. SAB has approximately 90 part\- and full\-time employees and an operating budget of $17 million. In the 2025\-2026 school year, administrative employees are expected to work in person 4 days per week and may telecommute one day per work week.

**Position Overview**


The School of American Ballet (SAB) seeks a Director of Institutional Giving to lead and expand its robust institutional giving program, comprised of foundation, government, and corporate foundation giving components. As a member of the School’s development staff, the Director of Institutional Giving will be responsible for raising over $1\.5 million annually, plus additional capital and endowment fundraising as needed. This position leads and grows the School's institutional fundraising and is a leader and resource for department\-wide staff and volunteers. The Director of Institutional Giving directly supervises and mentors one staff member. This is a full\-time, exempt position reporting to the Chief Development and Marketing Officer.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Institutional Giving**

* Manage and expand the School’s institutional giving strategy to secure more than $1\.5 million, with gifts ranging from $1,000 to $250,000\+.
* Build and manage relationships with 40\+ foundations, corporate, and government donors to ensure strong engagement with SAB and steward lasting support.
* Identify and strategically cultivate institutional prospects; implement tailored engagement strategies; solicit and secure gifts personally and as part of a team; and steward donors to maintain and strengthen long\-term relationships.
* Work closely with SAB\-wide staff to conceive of and submit persuasive, well\-written, and applicable proposals and reports, with accompanying budgets and support materials, on behalf of student life programming, the scholarship fund, and other priority initiatives.
* Oversee a comprehensive donor communication strategy, ensuring timely and high\-quality engagement through acknowledgement letters, written correspondence, invitations, mailings, visits, calls, newsletters, and e\-blasts.
* Develop strong relationships with Board members and coworkers; engage the Board’s Development Committee in cultivating and stewarding institutional donors; and serve as a resource to the Board and senior leadership team in their fundraising efforts.
* Guide prospect solicitation and donor stewardship efforts by the Executive Director and Board through the preparation of research, talking points, email drafts, and meeting briefings.
* Partner on the planning, execution, and fundraising for future capital and endowment campaigns.

**Supervision**

* Mentor, train, and supervise staff in Institutional Giving to ensure that departmental goals and needs are being met, and that staff are continually developing in their roles.
* Oversee the work conducted on behalf of Institutional Giving by department staff and volunteers.
* Supervise the maintenance of tracking systems, Institutional Giving mailing lists, and electronic and physical donor records.
* Manage Institutional Giving’s expense budget.

  

**Requirements** **Qualifications**

* 5\+ years of demonstrated success in institutional giving; knowledge of New York area funders.
* Excellent written and oral communication skills; fluency in budgeting and data analysis; ability to manage time and projects in a fast\-paced environment.
* Proven track record of securing institutional gifts at the $100,000\+ level.
* Polished and professional demeanor, with the ability to speak on behalf of the School at events.
* Proficiency in Raiser’s Edge or a similar donor database.
* Tasks might include some lifting, including heavy items that require use of carts.
* Evening and weekend hours required for donor events.

  

**Benefits**  

SAB offers a superior benefit package, including full health benefits, four weeks of vacation (plus two holiday weeks in December), and generous retirement savings benefits.


The School of American Ballet is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Diverse candidates are encouraged to apply.


The annual salary range is $100,000\-$112,000\.

jobs.title: Executive Director, NWSL Foundation
jobs.description:
The National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) is one of the fastest\-growing professional sports leagues in the U.S., powered by 16 clubs and a deep roster of the world’s best players, and built on record\-shattering fan, media and commercial growth. Now in its 14th season, the league’s momentum continues to accelerate, with viewership and attendance numbers growing rapidly, social media fandom on the rise, team valuations massively increasing and new top sponsors investing in the NWSL brand. This unprecedented growth in audience, media reach, and franchise value reflects the NWSL’s expanding fan base and increasing dominance in the sports\-media landscape and popular culture.

  

The future of the NWSL is now — and we’re looking for world\-class talent like you to help us continue the momentum.

 **About the NWSL Foundation**


The NWSL Foundation exists to advance the health and longevity of women athletes by supporting women’s health research and convening and coordinating the women’s athletic health research ecosystem. The Foundation helps guide the research agenda to ensure critical questions are identified, research efforts are aligned across institutions, and findings are translated into practical insights and resources for the benefit of the public and women and girls who participate in athletics.


The Foundation’s role is not to replicate academic research or function primarily as a grantmaker. Instead, it serves as a field\-shaping platform—aligning researchers, practitioners, and funders; reducing redundancy; elevating rigor; ensuring practical application, and enabling research that meaningfully advances women athletes’ health, performance, and longevity.


Anchored by an initial endowment, the Foundation will operate with scientific independence, disciplined governance, and a clear focus on actionability.

**Role Overview**


The Executive Director is the founding leader and public face of the NWSL Foundation. This role is accountable for setting and stewarding the research agenda, convening the ecosystem, and ensuring the Foundation earns credibility as a trusted leader in women’s athletic health research.


The Executive Director is not expected to be a career researcher or a traditional frontline fundraiser. Instead, this role requires a leader who has worked closely with researchers, clinicians, funders, and institutional partners—and who understands what it takes to develop credible research agendas, synthesize complex information, and mobilize resources in service of impact.


The Executive Director must be equally comfortable engaging senior researchers and clinicians, league and club leadership, players, and donors. This role requires judgment, credibility, and the ability to direct complex, multi\-stakeholder conversations—not simply administer programs.


The Executive Director reports to the NWSL Foundation Board and partners closely with League leadership, including Sporting and High Performance, while preserving scientific independence.

### **What You Will Own \& Drive**


1\. Research Agenda Leadership \& Field Stewardship

* Own and steward the Foundation’s multi\-year research agenda, grounded in elite women athlete needs and informed by the global research landscape.
* Identify gaps, redundancies, and under\-resourced areas across women’s athletic health research.
* Guide prioritization of research questions to ensure relevance, rigor, and actionability.
* Serve as an authoritative voice in shaping norms, priorities, and standards across the field—drawing credibility from prior leadership experience at the intersection of research, sport, and institutions.


2\. Convening \& Ecosystem Coordination

* Design and lead flagship convenings, including an annual research symposium that brings together leading researchers, clinicians, practitioners, and funders.
* Facilitate alignment and collaboration across academic institutions that are currently operating in parallel.
* Create structured forums for debate, synthesis, and agenda validation.
* Position the Foundation as a coordinator and catalyst—not a competitor to academic institutions.


3\. Research Governance, Rigor \& Independence

* Establish and oversee research governance structures, including Research Advisory Committees and peer review standards.
* Ensure funded, endorsed, or elevated research meets high standards of scientific rigor and ethical integrity.
* Protect scientific independence while maintaining relevance to elite sport environments.
* Define clear criteria for when and how research may involve NWSL athletes.


4\. Actionability \& Translation

* Ensure research questions and outputs are designed to be usable in practice, not solely academic.
* Partner with High Performance and Medical leadership to pressure\-test relevance and applicability.
* Support responsible translation of validated research into guidance, frameworks, or insights—without compromising independence or competitive integrity.


5\. Athlete\-Involved Research Oversight

* Establish disciplined protocols for research involving NWSL players, prioritizing player welfare, consent, and trust.
* Evaluate when athlete participation meaningfully advances the research agenda.
* Coordinate closely with League leadership, clubs, and the Players Association as appropriate.


6\. Fundraising \& External Partnerships

* Lead fundraising to sustain and scale the Foundation’s agenda\-setting work, including major gifts, aligned corporate partnerships, and research\-restricted funding.
* Inspire donors around impact, credibility, and long\-term field leadership—not transactional grantmaking.
* Develop integrated league moments (e.g., marquee convenings, designated matchweeks) that support fundraising without diluting mission.
* Represent the Foundation to philanthropic, academic, and institutional partners.


7\. Governance, Board \& Operations

* Build and manage a high\-functioning Foundation Board and committee structure (Audit, Research

jobs.title: Director of Communications and Strategic Partnerships - Beginnings Fund
jobs.description:
**Company Description** **Beginnings Fund**


POSITION: Director of Communications and Strategic Partnerships


REPORTS TO: CEO, Beginnings Fund


FLSA STATUS: Full\-time, Exempt


SALARY RANGE: $120,000 \- $160,000 USD


LOCATION: Remote – New York, London or Nairobi


WEBSITE: https://www.beginningsfund.org

 **Background**


Every year in Africa, 182,000 mothers die from preventable pregnancy\- and childbirth\-related causes, 950,000 babies are stillborn, and 1\.2 million newborns die. Global progress against maternal and newborn mortality has stalled in recent years, and most African countries are not on track to meet the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals for maternal and newborn survival.


The Beginnings Fund is a philanthropic initiative that accelerates maternal and newborn survival in Africa by investing, in partnership with governments, in the products, people, and systems needed to sustainably improve care at scale. During its first five years, the Beginnings Fund will focus on Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Ghana, Lesotho, Uganda, and Zimbabwe. Investments are developed and managed by a majority\-Africa\-based Investment Team, led by a Nairobi\-based CEO who reports to an Investment Committee composed of the founding and anchor investors in the Beginnings Fund.


While the fund's initial phase is five years, the broader ambition is to raise $1 billion over ten years to expand into additional countries, with the potential to grow into a long\-term collaborative fund.


The Beginnings Fund is fiscally sponsored by Global Impact.

 **Job Description**  

Reporting to the CEO, the Director of Communications and Strategic Partnerships will lead a dual\-focus role shaping how the Fund engages its investors and audiences, builds its reputation, and delivers on its mission. You will also serve as a senior advisor on communications, positioning, and reputational risk, ensuring the Fund’s voice is clear, consistent, and aligned with its vision and values.


In addition to serving as a master storyteller with sharp financial and developmental acumen, the Director will be responsible for demonstrating how strategic philanthropic capital translates into systems\-level healthcare transformation across Africa and for stewarding key relationships to sustain and scale.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1\. Investor Relations and Stewardship**

* **Investor Relations:** Manage relationships with current and prospective philanthropic investors, family offices, and institutional donors, keeping them deeply connected to the fund’s progress and strategic outlook, including but not limited to virtual and written updates, investor events, and formal annual reporting.
* **Fiscal Sponsor Alignment:** Coordinate closely with Global Impact to ensure all financial reporting, grant tracking, and compliance communications are seamless and accurate.
* **Fundraising:** Partner with the CEO to develop sophisticated fundraising materials and investment cases for future funding rounds.
* **Investment Committee Reporting:** Support the development of high\-quality investor reports, comprehensive performance, financial, and impact updates for the Investment Committee
* **Co\-Investment:** develop a highly efficient co\-investment program for investors with varying needs, including those who may not wish to invest in the pooled fund and/or may wish to invest in specific countries or areas of work through earmarked or restricted contributions, as well as for new partners of the Fund.
* **Strategic Meetings \& Executive Engagement**: Support the CEO in her engagement with global conferences and strategic meetings, ensuring seamless alignment between high\-level leadership engagements and donor stewardship goals.
* **Investor Events**: Coordinate investor events annually to foster engagement, highlight fund achievements, and deepen donor relationships.

**2\. Strategic Communications \& Policy Advocacy**

* **Narrative Ownership:** Craft and protect the Beginnings Fund narrative, positioning the initiative as a collaborative, Africa\-driven authority on maternal and newborn health systems.
* **Government \& Partner Communications:** Support the Investment Team in shaping communications for ministry\-level government partners to foster trust, transparency, and sustainable co\-investment.
* **Multi\-Channel Content Creation:** Oversee the fund's digital footprint including managing and updating the website, developing high\-level insights, op\-eds, press releases, and digital media that speak to global development audiences and regional stakeholders.
* **Media \& Public Relations:** Build and maintain strong relationships with key regional and international journalists covering global health, philanthropy, and African development to keep maternal and newborn survival at the top of the global agenda.

**3\. Country\-Level Impact Storytelling**

* Work hand\-in\-hand with the Africa\-based Investment Team to extract complex clinical and system\-level metrics (e.g., product deployment, training scale, mortality reductions) and translate them into human\-centric success stories.
* **Regional Events:** Lead planning and communication for major milestones, including regional summits, donor field visits, and panels at major global health convenings (such as the World Health Assembly or the African Union Summit).

  

**Qualifications**  

* **Experience: 7–10**\+ years of experience in Investor Relations, Strategic Communications, Philanthropic Development, or Public Affairs. Experience working within venture philanthropy, impact investing, or large\-scale global health initiatives in Africa is highly preferred.
* **Regional Expertise:** A deep understanding of the developmental, political, and healthcare landscapes across Sub\-Saharan Africa, with specific familiarity with one or more of our target countries (Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Ghana, Lesotho, Uganda, Zimbabwe).
* **Storytelling \& Data Master

jobs.title: Associate Executive Director
jobs.description:
Take the next step in your career with this rewarding opportunity to join the YMCA of South Hampton Roads.
Job Description
Under the direction of the Executive Director, the Associate Executive Director is responsible for overseeing the daily operations. This position provides cause\-driven leadership in staff supervision, volunteer management, fiscal oversight, financial development, program administration, facility and equipment stewardship, community relations, and personal and professional development.


Qualifications
* Strong business operations background with a proven track record for producing growth, annual giving and strong financial management
* A Bachelor's Degree in a child related field or Sports Management/ Recreation/Health Sciences is preferred, or 48 semester hours or 72 quarter hours of college credit of which 12 semester hours or 18 quarter hours are in subjects relating to children.
* Five or more years of successful management experience, preferably in a YMCA or other nonprofit agency in the health \& wellness, business or related field
* Supervision of full and part\-time employees and accountability for annual budget exceeding $1 million
* Ability to lead assigned operations including staff development and supervision, development and monitoring of budgets, membership and program development, financial development, marketing and public relations, board and volunteer development
* Ability to establish and maintain collaborations with community organizations
* YMCA Multi\-Team Leader certification preferred
**WORKING CONDITIONS:**

* This role requires daily onsite work and occasional after\-hours response; therefore, candidates must be able to reliably commute to the assigned location and reside within approximately 30 miles or 45 minutes of the worksite by their start date to meet operational needs
* Requires a person of maturity and good judgment, who can operate with a minimum of guidance from the Division Vice President
* Requires ability to exercise appropriate independent judgment, to assess facts and issues, and make non\-routine decisions regarding day\-to\-day operational problems and issues
* Requires effective team\-building and team\-leadership skills
* Must maintain cooperative, functional relationships with senior leadership team, peers, and subordinates
* Must maintain positive, energetic attitude toward YMCA work, goals, and values
* Must have ability to respond to emergencies 24 hours a day, and to travel as needed for operational management, including on\-site presence in managing major operational problems
* Must have superior oral and written communication skills and the ability to respond to a wide variety of constituencies, including staff, volunteers, members, program participants, vendors, community leaders, etc.
* Performs the duties of direct reports as needed

**ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS, PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:**

* Physically able to successfully complete required job functions, including use of hands, arms, fingers, able to talk and hear, use a computer, sit and stand, regularly move/lift up to 50 pounds, enter all YMCA environments (office spaces, indoor and outdoor maintenance/mechanical areas, fitness areas, pool and pool space, camping areas, unimproved outdoor locations and other program areas)
* Continuous operations requiring attention to detail and multi\-tasking
* Physically able to successfully complete required certifications
Essential Functions
**Division of Duties:**

* 65% Direct leadership of all day\-to\-day operations
* 20% \- Property Management
* 10% \- Leadership role in the Annual Impact Fund
* 5% \- Staff development of direct reports

**Priorities**

* Supervise all the day\-to\-day operations of the assigned location.
* Develop, manage, and achieve the budget expectations with an emphasis on licensed childcare programs, Events and Rentals, Sports and Aquatic programming, Community Relations, and Fundraising.
* Assist with all fundraising efforts with an emphasis on staff and community giving.
* Support board development by assisting the Executive Director in recruiting three new board members annually and leading a board subcommittee.
* Oversee property management, ensuring the upkeep of all grounds and facilities.
* Foster relationship development with key home office leaders, including VPs of various product lines.

**Budget and Financial Performance**

* Develop, manage, and monitor operating budgets to meet or exceed targets.
* Initiate adjustments to operations to ensure a balanced budget.
* Ensure completion of monthly variance reports and forecasting.

**Program Development and Membership Engagement**

* Implements Association childcare strategies that support recruitment of new participants and retention of existing participants. Creates a member\-focused culture and models relationship\-building skills in all interactions. Uses YMCA “listen first” skills to understand and respond to the needs, wants and interests of participants. Fosters a climate of innovation and resolves problems to ensure participant satisfaction
* Develops long\-range plans for the expansion of programs and services in harmony with overall YMCA objectives.
* Monitors the achievements of these objectives and exercises appropriate action to assure the achievements of the objectives are of the highest quality programs and services
* Represents and promotes the YMCA in the local community by developing positive working and collaborative relationships with other organizations, businesses, and governmental entities
* Ensures safety, cleanliness, and function of all related facilities and equipment

**Team Performance Toward Organizational Goals**

* Development and supervision of the Family Center operations
* Recruits, hires, trains, develops, and leads employees and volunteers. Reviews and evaluates staff performance.
* Develops strategies to motivate staff and achieve goals. Responsible for supervision of exempt and non exempt employees
*

*This represents the full pay range for the position; most new hires can expect an offer between the minimum and midpoint of the range, depending on experience.*

 **ABOUT COMMUNITIES IN SCHOOLS OF WASHINGTON**


For over 30 years, Communities In Schools of Washington (CISWA), in partnership with the 12 local network affiliates across Washington state, has been striving for equity in educational opportunities. The state office is a small, high\-energy office that has a history of strong operations and successful outcomes built upon community partnerships. Driven by our core values of collaboration, opportunity, access, and transformation and in adherence to the CIS National guidelines, the state office works to ensure that all affiliates and their Boards of Directors have the tools and capacity to provide and sustain strong student programs and services in their local communities as they work directly inside K\-12 schools supporting students who have historically been furthest from educational justice.

 **JOB SUMMARY**


The Development Director leads the CISWA State Office’s resource development strategy, creating and executing comprehensive multi\-year and annual fundraising plans to meet ambitious revenue goals. Reporting to the State Executive Director, this role manages the Development team, directly oversees fundraising for the State Office and two in\-house affiliates, leverages board member engagement, and provides consultative leadership to strengthen fundraising capacity across Washington’s CIS affiliate network. The ideal candidate brings 7\+ years of relevant nonprofit resource development expertise (equivalent combination of education and experience), a strong work ethic and drive for excellence, and a commitment to equity, collaboration, and youth\-centered practice in alignment with our organizational values.

* Pursue ongoing professional development and industry training to stay current on fundraising trends in the nonprofit and local community.

**Capacity Building for Statewide Affiliate Networ****k**

jobs.title: President & CEO
jobs.description:
**Lead the Voice of Business in Interior Alaska**

The Greater Fairbanks Chamber of Commerce is seeking a proven executive leader to serve as its next President and Chief Executive Officer.

This is an opportunity to lead one of Alaska’s most influential regional business organizations at an important time for Interior Alaska. The Chamber represents a diverse membership of nearly 600 businesses and organizations and serves as a trusted advocate, convener, and strategic partner for the regional business community.

The President and CEO is the Chamber’s chief executive, lead advocate, primary spokesperson, and senior relationship builder. Working with the Board of Directors, the CEO translates the Chamber’s mission and strategic priorities into measurable results while ensuring strong organizational systems, accountability, and financial discipline.

The next CEO will join an organization with an engaged Board, committed staff, strong community relationships, respected advocacy programs, and established signature events. The Board is focused on strengthening internal systems, staff development, financial reporting, strategic execution, member value, and long\-term revenue stability.

**Immediate Leadership Priorities**

The next President and CEO will be expected to:

* Strengthen organizational systems, accountability, and performance reporting
* Develop and lead a high\-performing staff team
* Ensure strong financial stewardship and sustainable revenue growth
* Strengthen membership engagement, recruitment, retention, and value
* Advance a credible, nonpartisan, pro\-business advocacy agenda
* Build productive relationships with business leaders, elected officials, military partners, Alaska Native organizations, educators, media, and community stakeholders
* Maintain a visible and credible presence throughout the Fairbanks business community

**Scope of Leadership**

The President and CEO provides executive leadership in the following areas:

* Strategic and operational planning
* Administration and staff management
* Board and committee relations
* Advocacy and public policy
* External relations and partnerships
* Communications, marketing, and media relations
* Financial management and organizational sustainability
* Revenue development
* Membership growth and value

The CEO serves as a non\-voting member of the Board of Directors and Executive Committee and performs the duties assigned to the position under the Chamber’s bylaws.

**Experience \& Qualifications**

The successful candidate should bring:

* Significant senior leadership experience in business, nonprofit, government, public affairs, economic development, a membership organization, or a related environment
* Experience working effectively with a governing board and maintaining clear distinctions between governance and management
* Proven success leading staff, setting expectations, developing talent, managing performance, and building a healthy workplace culture
* Experience managing an organizational or departmental budget of at least $1 million
* Demonstrated success generating revenue through membership, sponsorships, events, partnerships, grants, fundraising, or other earned\-income strategies
* Experience building productive relationships with business leaders, elected officials, community partners, media, and diverse constituencies
* Ability to navigate legislative, regulatory, and political processes; direct advocacy or public policy experience is strongly preferred
* Strong written, public speaking, media, facilitation, and interpersonal communication skills

A bachelor’s degree in business, public administration, communications, political science, nonprofit management, or a related field is preferred. Equivalent education, executive leadership experience, and demonstrated achievement may be considered.

**Leadership Characteristics**

The Chamber seeks a leader who is:

* Organized, disciplined, and consistent in follow\-through
* Strategic while attentive to operational detail
* Transparent, responsive, and proactive in communication
* Confident and diplomatic across differing viewpoints
* Collaborative, decisive, and willing to address difficult issues
* Politically astute and able to advance a nonpartisan, Board\-approved agenda
* Committed to building trust and becoming an active member of the Fairbanks community

**Compensation \& Benefits**

The Chamber offers a competitive compensation package that includes:

* **Base salary:** $140,000 to $180,000, depending on qualifications and experience
* Eligibility for an annual performance incentive
* Relocation assistance, which may be available as part of the final compensation package
* Medical, dental, and vision coverage, with the Chamber paying 75% of employee premiums
* SIMPLE IRA with an employer match of up to 3% of eligible compensation
* Four weeks of combined paid time off annually
* Paid holidays and floating holidays

This is a full\-time, Fairbanks\-based executive position. The role requires occasional early\-morning, evening, and weekend commitments, along with periodic travel within and outside Alaska.

The President and CEO is an at\-will employee of the Greater Fairbanks Chamber of Commerce.

**About Fairbanks**

Fairbanks is the economic, military, education, healthcare, transportation, and cultural hub of Interior Alaska. The region offers leaders the opportunity to make a visible impact while building meaningful relationships across business, government, education, the military, Alaska Native organizations, and civic life.

Residents enjoy year\-round recreation, a vibrant arts and cultural community, convenient air access, and the distinctive rhythms of Alaska’s seasons, from summer’s midnight sun to winter’s aurora.

**How to Apply**

Qualified candidates should apply online at **fairbankschamber.org/careers** and submit:

* A cover letter describing their interest in the position and relevant experience
* A current résumé
* Contact informa

jobs.title: Director of Marketing and Communications
jobs.description:
Hillel Academy of Pittsburgh is a growing Orthodox Jewish day school serving students from Early Childhood through Grade 12 on the Yitzy Sutofsky Campus. We provide an exceptional Orthodox Jewish and general studies education in a warm, nurturing environment that prepares students to become thoughtful, accomplished, and committed members of the Jewish community and broader society. We are seeking an experienced, creative, and mission\-driven Director of Marketing and Communications to lead the school’s strategic marketing, branding, institutional storytelling, and communications efforts. Working closely with the CEO, COO, Principal and Educational Director, and other administrators, this individual will strengthen Hillel Academy’s brand, support enrollment and fundraising, and communicate the school’s impact to families, donors, alumni, and the broader community.


STRATEGY


Lead integrated marketing and brand strategy.


STORYTELLING


Showcase the impact of a Hillel Academy education.


GROWTH


Support enrollment, fundraising, and engagement.


Key Responsibilities

* Strategic Marketing \& Brand Leadership: Develop and execute an integrated strategy aligned with the school’s


mission, strategic priorities, enrollment goals, and fundraising objectives; safeguard the Hillel Academy brand and advise senior leadership on communications.

* Enrollment \& Advancement Marketing: Create campaigns and materials that support student recruitment and retention, annual and capital fundraising, donor stewardship, alumni engagement, and major institutional initiatives.
* Institutional Storytelling \& Community Engagement: Share compelling stories about students, faculty, alumni, Jewish life, academics, athletics, arts, STEM, and community service; strengthen relationships with families, donors, community partners, and media.
* Digital, Creative \& Communications Oversight: Oversee the website, social media, email, print, video, photography, advertising, newsletters, press releases, event promotions, and branded materials; maintain consistent quality and messaging across platforms.
* Internal \& Crisis Communications: Support clear internal communications and assist senior leadership with sensitive, urgent, or crisis\-related messaging, talking points, parent notices, FAQs, and public statements.
* Analytics \& Operations: Monitor engagement and campaign performance, manage communications budgets and vendors, and create systems that keep projects accurate, efficient, and on schedule.


Qualifications

* Bachelor’s degree in marketing, communications, public relations, journalism, English, business, or a related field preferred.
* Professional experience in marketing, communications, branding, public relations, advancement communications, or a related field.
* Exceptional writing, editing, proofreading, storytelling, project management, and strategic communications skills.
* Experience with websites, email marketing, social media, print materials, multimedia content, and integrated campaigns.
* Excellent judgment, discretion, organization, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders.


Hillel Academy of Pittsburgh • Director of Marketing and Communications

* Independent school, Jewish communal, nonprofit, educational, or other mission\-driven experience strongly preferred.
* Knowledge of Orthodox Jewish practices, culture and values, Jewish day school education, and the Pittsburgh Jewish community required.


The Ideal Candidate


The successful candidate will be strategic, creative, highly organized, collaborative, responsive, and service\-oriented. This person will be comfortable balancing long\-term planning with immediate communications needs and will be passionate about Orthodox Jewish education and the impact of Hillel Academy.

jobs.title: Development Director
jobs.description:
Deborah's Place is Chicago's largest provider of supportive housing dedicated to serving women experiencing homelessness. Our mission is to open doors of opportunity by providing safe, stable housing and comprehensive supportive services that foster healing, recovery, and independence.


We are seeking an experienced and relationship\-driven Development Director to lead our fundraising strategy, strengthen donor engagement, and expand philanthropic support for our mission. Report to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), the Development Director provides strategic leadership for the organization's development program and works closely with the Board of Directors, staff, donors, and community partners to secure the resources needed to advance our work.

**Position Summary**


The Development Director provides leadership and oversight for all functions of the Development Department, with primary responsibility for cultivating and soliciting individual donors and prospects, growing the annual giving program, and expanding major gift philanthropy. The Director develops and implements fundraising strategies that strengthen donor relationships, increase philanthropic support, and advance the organization's strategic priorities.


Working in partnership with the CEO and Board of Directors, the Development Director leads fundraising planning and execution while fostering a culture of philanthropy throughout the organization.

**Key Responsibilities**

***Fundraising Leadership***

* Develop and implement the organization's annual fundraising plan and department budget.
* Lead strategies to grow annual giving, major gifts, and planned giving.
* Identify, cultivate, solicit, recognize, and steward individual donors and major gift prospects.
* Develop donor engagement strategies that increase donor acquisition, retention, and giving.
* Lead fundraising initiatives to support annual operating priorities and capital campaigns, when applicable.
* Monitor fundraising performance and recommend strategies to achieve revenue goals.

***Board \& Donor Engagement***

* Staff the Board Resource Development Committee and partner with Board members to strengthen fundraising efforts.
* Work closely with the Chief Executive Officer and Board of Directors to cultivate and solicit major donors.
* Build and maintain strong relationships with donors, foundations, community leaders, and philanthropic partners.
* Support Board engagement in fundraising, stewardship, and ambassador activities.
* Provide oversight of the Young Professionals Board through supervision of the staff liaison.

***Department Leadership***

* Provide leadership, direction, and supervision to Development Department staff.
* Foster a collaborative, high\-performing team focused on donor stewardship, fundraising excellence, and continuous improvement.
* Ensure effective coordination of fundraising campaigns, donor communications, stewardship activities, events, and development operations.
* Establish department priorities, monitor progress toward goals, and support professional development of staff.

***Organizational Leadership***

* Serve as a member of the agency's leadership team and contribute to strategic planning and organizational decision\-making.
* Participate in annual planning, budgeting, and long\-term organizational initiatives.
* Represent Deborah's Place with donors, volunteers, community organizations, and external stakeholders.
* Promote the organization's mission, values, and commitment to serving women experiencing homelessness.

 **Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in nonprofit management, communications, marketing, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
* 5 or more years of nonprofit fundraising experience, including major gifts and donor cultivation.
* Demonstrated success securing and stewarding major gifts.
* Experience developing and implementing annual fundraising strategies.
* Experience working with nonprofit boards and volunteer leaders.
* Supervisory and team leadership experience.
* Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.
* Experience with Raiser's Edge NXT or a comparable donor database.
* Experience leading annual giving, capital, or planned giving initiatives.
* Knowledge of the Chicago philanthropic community.

 **Why Join Deborah's Place?**


This is an opportunity to lead philanthropy for an organization that has transformed the lives of thousands of women experiencing homelessness. You'll join a dedicated leadership team, work alongside an engaged Board of Directors, and help shape the future of an organization with a strong reputation for innovation, compassion, and impact.

*Deborah's Place is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds and lived experiences to apply.*

jobs.title: President & Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
The Greater Baton Rouge Economic Partnership, formerly the Baton Rouge Area Chamber, is searching for its next President and Chief Executive Officer.


The Partnership is the regional economic development organization for Louisiana's nine\-parish Capital Region. We represent more than 500 business investors and work to expand economic opportunity, strengthen the talent pipeline, support business growth and industry diversification, advance competitive public policy, and improve quality of place across the region.


This is a national search. Local candidates are welcome and encouraged to apply.


Why this role matters right now


Our current five\-year strategy, BRING IT! Baton Rouge, ends at the close of 2026\. The next President and CEO will work with the Board of Directors, investors, staff, and regional partners to set the organization's next strategic direction. You are not stepping into a caretaker job. You are setting the plan.


What you will do

* Lead the organization's strategy, operations, staff, and budget, subject to Board direction.
* Serve as a leading public voice for the Capital Region with business leaders, elected officials, media, and national partners.
* Set and drive the regional business community's public policy and advocacy agenda at the local, state, and federal levels.
* Build and manage relationships with more than 500 investors and with regional, state, and federal partners.
* Lead the development of the organization's next economic development strategic plan.
* Manage roughly 8 direct reports and a staff of 30 across six business units.
* Oversee an operating budget of about $8 million and remain accountable to the Board for sound financial management.


The President and CEO reports to the Board of Directors through the Board Chairperson.


What we are looking for

* At least 10 years of executive leadership experience in an organization of comparable size and complexity.
* Working knowledge of economic development, public policy, business leadership, chamber leadership, or a related field. IEDC or ACCE background preferred.
* A track record of results in a complex environment with many stakeholders.
* Experience managing a large board and investor or member relationships.
* A credible public voice, with real experience in government relations and advocacy.
* Full budget ownership experience, including nonprofit financial compliance.
* Bachelor's degree required. Advanced degree preferred.

The South Dakota Historical Society Foundation is a nonprofit 501(c)(3\) organization dedicated to preserving and sharing the rich history of South Dakota. info@sdhsf.org

**Priority consideration will be given to applications received by September 30, 2026\.**

Pay: $85,000\.00 \- $95,000\.00 per year

**ABOUT THE MUHAMMAD ALI CENTER** 

The Muhammad Ali Center was created to honor the life of “The Greatest”. Based in Louisville, KY, the Center is a multicultural organization, an award\-winning museum, and a global beacon for social justice. We exist to mobilize Ali’s legacy to foster respect, inspire generations of changemakers, and advance social justice, creating a world where all people can achieve their own greatness.

From the Ali Center's inception, Diversity, Equity, \& Inclusion have been central to our core values. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer that believes diverse viewpoints are critical to our global impact, and we actively foster a culture where inclusion is everyone’s responsibility.

**POSITION OVERVIEW:**

The President \& Chief Executive Officer (CEO) will provide the visionary leadership, strategic direction, and operational oversight required to champion the Ali Center’s mission and drive its next phase of global growth. Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the CEO holds full executive authority and accountability for all Center operations, including a $5M operating budget, a dedicated team of 30\+ staff and volunteers, programming and the operations of our world\-class facility.

As a primary public face of the Center, the CEO will convert mission into measurable global results. A proven track record of high\-level fundraising is paramount; the CEO will spearhead philanthropic growth across individual, corporate, foundational, and government sectors to ensure long\-term financial sustainability.

**Revenue Generation \& Sustainability**

· **Partnership \& Alliance Building**: Skilled at building consensus among diverse stakeholders, including board members, elected officials, community leaders, and international partners.

* Fundraising: 10 years (Required)

**About Amyloidosis Research Consortium**


The Amyloidosis Research Consortium (ARC) is a 501c(3\) nonprofit organization founded in 2015, harnessing the power of collaboration and innovation to advance science and both improve and extend the lives of those with Amyloidosis. We are dedicated to transforming the way research is being done and focus on what will have the most significant impact on improving the lives of amyloidosis patients. We forge collaborations across industry, research, clinical care, and regulatory to address unmet needs and accelerate the discovery of new treatments. ARC empowers and supports patients by ensuring they have access to the best quality care and information.

  

Amyloidosis is a group of diseases where abnormal proteins build up in organs, causing progressive damage. In the U.S., approximately 3,800 new AL amyloidosis cases are diagnosed annually. However, ATTR amyloidosis affects far more people: over 100,000 Americans have the age\-related form, and 50,000 people worldwide have the inherited form. Studies show that roughly 13% of older heart failure patients actually have undiagnosed ATTR amyloidosis, meaning the true patient population is even larger. As awareness and diagnosis improve, the community continues to grow.

  

To learn more about ARC, visit http://www.arci.org.

The **Director of Communications and Marketing** leads communications for ARC and serves as a strategic partner to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and department leads. **JOB DESCRIPTION**

**Position Title:** Chief Operating Officer (COO)

**Reports To:** Chief Executive Officer

**Department:** Executive Leadership

**Status:** Exempt

**Date:** July 2026

 **Broad Functions:** The Chief Operating Officer (COO) provides operational and financial leadership for the company's portfolio of restaurant and retail concessions located in airports and travel plazas across the United States. Operating nearly 400 locations across 27 airports and 12 travel plazas nationwide, the company is one of the largest privately held travel hospitality operators in the United States and the U.S. division of Areas, a global leader in travel hospitality. 7\. **About the Israeli\-American Council (IAC)**


The mission of the IAC is to build an engaged and united Israeli\-American community that strengthens the Israeli and Jewish identity of the next generations, the American Jewish community, and the bond between the peoples of the United States and the State of Israel.

 **Position Overview**

  

The **Director of Development** is a senior fundraising professional responsible for leading all philanthropic activities within an assigned region. This individual develops and executes a comprehensive regional fundraising strategy, manages a portfolio of major donors and prospects, and works closely with Regional Directors, volunteer leadership, and the national Development team to achieve ambitious fundraising goals. The Director of Development serves as a strategic partner to regional leadership and acts as a trusted advisor to donors, helping them align their philanthropic interests with the IAC’s mission and priorities. This is an entrepreneurial, externally facing role requiring exceptional relationship\-building skills, strategic thinking, and a demonstrated ability to secure transformational philanthropic investments. The Director of Development reports to the **Chief Communities \& Growth Officer** and works closely with Regional Directors and senior organizational leadership.

 **Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:** **Regional Fundraising Strategy**

* Develop and implement the annual regional development plan aligned with the IAC’s national fundraising priorities.
* Identify new philanthropic opportunities and expand the regional donor pipeline.
* Analyze fundraising performance and adjust strategies to maximize results.
* Create annual revenue forecasts and monitor progress toward goals.

 **Major Gifts \& Donor Portfolio Management**

* Manage a portfolio of major donors and high\-capacity prospects through all stages of moves management, including identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and renewal.
* Develop and execute individualized strategies to secure five\-, six\-, and seven\-figure gifts.
* Meet or exceed annual fundraising goals and key performance indicators.
* Build long\-term relationships with philanthropists, family foundations, corporations, donor\-advised funds, and community leaders.
* Prepare compelling proposals, gift agreements, stewardship reports, and impact communications.

 **Donor Engagement \& Stewardship**

* Design and execute meaningful donor stewardship plans that strengthen engagement and inspire increased giving.
* Partner with senior leadership to cultivate strategic donor relationships.
* Represent the IAC at donor meetings, community gatherings, and regional events.
* Serve as a passionate ambassador for the organization’s mission and impact.

 **Events \& Community Engagement**

* Lead fundraising strategy for regional galas, leadership receptions, parlor meetings, donor briefings, and mission\-related events.
* Collaborate with Regional Directors and volunteer leadership to maximize sponsorships, ticket sales, and philanthropic giving.
* Leverage events as opportunities to cultivate new donors and deepen existing relationships.

 **Development Operations**

* Maintain accurate donor records, moves management activities, and revenue forecasts in the organization’s CRM.
* Utilize data and analytics to guide fundraising strategy and portfolio management.
* Prepare reports, dashboards, and pipeline updates for senior leadership.

 **Skills/Qualifications**  

* Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree or CFRE certification preferred.
* Minimum of **7 years of progressively responsible fundraising experience**, including major gifts.
* Demonstrated success securing and closing five\-, six\-, and preferably seven\-figure philanthropic gifts.
* Proven experience managing complex donor portfolios \& sophisticated moves management strategies.
* Strong understanding of principal gifts, annual giving, corporate partnerships, foundations, and planned giving opportunities.
* Exceptional interpersonal, communication, presentation, and negotiation skills.
* Experience working with high\-net\-worth individuals, volunteer leadership, and governing boards.
* Entrepreneurial mindset with outstanding organizational and project management skills.
* Highly self\-motivated with the ability to work independently while collaborating across departments.
* Advanced proficiency with CRM systems and fundraising analytics.
* Knowledge of the Israeli American and broader Jewish philanthropic community strongly preferred.
* Fluent English required; conversational Hebrew strongly preferred.
* Willingness to work evenings, weekends, and travel throughout the assigned region and nationally as needed.

 **Key Performance Indicators**


Success in this role will be measured by:

* Achievement of annual and quarterly fundraising revenue goals.
* Growth in major gift revenue.
* Expansion of the regional donor pipeline.
* Increased donor retention and donor upgrades.
* Successful acquisition of new major donors.
* Execution of high\-impact fundraising events.
* Accurate CRM management, reporting, and forecasting.
* Strengthened engagement of volunteer leadership and strategic partners.

 **Compensation \& Benefits**


The Israeli\-American Council offers a competitive compensation package, comprehensive health benefits, retirement plan, generous paid time off, professional development opportunities, and the chance to be part of one of North America’s fastest\-growing Jewish nonprofit organizations.


Salary is commensurate with experience and geographic market.

 **Why Join the IAC?**


Joining the IAC means becoming part of a mission\-driven organization that is shaping the future of the Israeli\-American and Jewish communities. You will work alongside passionate colleagues, visionary philanthropists, and community leaders to strengthen Jewish identity, inspire civic engagement, support I

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
**Job Summary**

We are seeking a dynamic and strategic Chief Operating Officer (COO) to lead our organization’s operational excellence and drive sustainable growth. As a key member of the executive leadership team, the COO will oversee daily business activities, optimize operational processes, and ensure alignment with our strategic objectives. This role demands a proactive leader with exceptional management skills, financial acumen, and a passion for developing high\-performing teams. The ideal candidate will be instrumental in shaping our business development initiatives, enhancing customer service standards, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement.

**Duties**

* Develop and implement comprehensive operational strategies aligned with overall business goals to maximize efficiency and profitability.
* Oversee profit \& loss management, conducting detailed analysis to inform strategic decision\-making and ensure financial health.
* Lead cross\-functional teams through effective management, team development, and leadership initiatives to cultivate a motivated and high\-performing workforce.
* Manage business operations by streamlining processes using lean management principles and driving process improvements across departments.
* Drive project management efforts for large\-scale initiatives, ensuring timely delivery within scope and budget while maintaining quality standards.
* Utilize Excel data analysis tools to monitor key performance indicators (KPIs), identify trends, and support data\-driven decision making.
* Foster strong managerial communication channels to facilitate transparency, collaboration, and effective problem\-solving at all levels.
* Lead strategic planning sessions to identify growth opportunities, optimize sales strategies, and expand business development efforts.
* Oversee operational management functions including customer service standards, vendor relations, and compliance adherence.
* Supervise executive\-level teams to ensure alignment on company objectives while promoting leadership development and team growth.

**Qualifications**

* Proven experience in management roles with a strong background in business management, operational oversight, and team leadership.
* Demonstrated success in profit \& loss analysis, financial management, and strategic planning within a fast\-paced environment.
* Expertise in Excel data analysis for monitoring KPIs, forecasting trends, and supporting data\-driven decisions.
* Extensive project management experience with a focus on process improvement and operational efficiency.
* Strong leadership skills with experience managing executive teams and supervising large groups of employees across multiple functions.
* Excellent managerial communication skills to effectively convey strategies, expectations, and feedback at all organizational levels.
* Knowledge of sales techniques, customer service excellence, and business development strategies.
* Familiarity with lean management principles and operational best practices to optimize workflows.
* Ability to develop teams through coaching, mentorship, and strategic talent acquisition to foster continuous growth.

Join us as our Chief Operating Officer if you’re ready to lead transformative change, inspire teams toward excellence, and shape the future of our organization through innovative operational strategies!

Pay: $200,000\.00 \- $260,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Employee assistance program
* Employee discount
* Health savings account
* Professional development assistance

Work Location: Remote

jobs.description:
**GEISINGER**

**DANVILLE, PENNSYLVANIA** **– HQ (HYBRID)**



HARTZ Search invites you to explore an exciting opportunity for the Chief Operating Officer, Insurance Operations, with our client, Geisinger, in Danville, PA. The Chief Operating Officer, Insurance Operations is responsible for leading, planning, and overseeing the operational strategy, performance, and execution of Geisinger's Insurance Operations functions. Geisinger Insurance Operations (GIO) includes Geisinger Health Plan, Geisinger Indemnity Insurance Company, and Geisinger Quality Operations.



Geisinger is among the nation’s leading providers of value\-based care, serving 1\.2 million people in rural and urban communities across central and northeastern Pennsylvania. Founded in 1915 by philanthropist Abigail Geisinger, the nonprofit system generates $9 billion in annual revenues across more than 130 care sites — including 10 hospital campuses — and Geisinger Health Plan, with 509,000\+ enrollees in commercial and government plans.



Geisinger College of Health Sciences educates more than 600 medical professionals annually and conducts more than 1,600 clinical research studies. With 28,000 employees, including 1,900 employed physicians and 5,400 registered nurses, Geisinger is among Pennsylvania’s largest employers with an estimated economic impact of $18 billion on the state’s economy. In 2024, Geisinger joined Risant Health, a nonprofit charitable organization created to expand and accelerate value\-based care across the country.


**JOB DESCRIPTION:**


* Responsible and accountable for successfully delivering the entire portfolio of GIO operational initiatives. Drives the changes to the processes and related system capabilities needed to facilitate the delivery of those initiatives across the organization.
* Ensures member\-centric culture and communications. Provides vision, organization, and leadership to the Customer Service, Claims, and Membership operations for the GIO. Responsible for compliance with state and federal regulatory requirements applicable to these operational areas.
* In conjunction with peers; provides vision, organization, and leadership in the implementation of activities around strategic planning, resource prioritization, resource coordination, budget forecasting, and effective communications to all appropriate levels.
* Responsible for driving the self\-service capabilities available to Members, Providers, and Employer Groups.
* Communicates and consults with GIO and Geisinger leadership with regard to the overall condition and performance of the GIO. Advises leadership regarding new programs / financial issues of these areas, making recommendations about the overall implications of a decision.
* Fosters and promotes a positive work environment with teamwork, respect, and communication; supports personal growth and development of people. Creates an environment of accountability, responsibility, and ownership through consistent leadership, direction, and support.
* Responsible for GIO oversight of the Human Resources function.


**ROLE DETAILS:**


* COO, Insurance Operations reports directly to the President of Geisinger Health Plan.
* The COO, Insurance Operations will have 6 direct reports.


**REQUIREMENTS \& QUALIFICATIONS:**


* Education:
	+ Bachelor’s Degree required
* Experience:
	+ Minimum of 10 years of healthcare experience.
	+ Minimum of 10 years of progressive leadership experience.

**LOCATION: DANVILLE, PENNSYLVANIA**



Danville is a quiet and charming town in Central Pennsylvania, located on the Susquehanna River, 50 miles west of Scranton and 100 miles from Philadelphia. Living in Danville, PA is a wonderful experience. The community is close\-knit and full of friendly faces. There are plenty of activities to keep you busy, such as local parks and trails, restaurants, shops, and entertainment venues. With its vibrant downtown area and plentiful outdoor recreation opportunities, there's something for everyone in Danville. On top of that, the town offers excellent schools and services, making it a great place to raise a family or start a business. No matter what type of lifestyle you're looking for, Danville has something to offer everyone.


**INTERESTED CANDIDATES, PLEASE APPLY DIRECTLY to HARTZ Search below:** *https://www.linkedin.com/company/hartz\-search/*


**Qualified candidates, please submit your current resume \- applications will not be considered without a resume. Thank you!**


**Application Link:** *https://hartzsearch.com/open\-position/chief\-operating\-officer\-insurance\-operations/*



HARTZ Search is a retained executive search firm that conducts searches for our healthcare and academic clients across the US. Our focus is on Talent, Communication, and Performance \- We stand apart in finding the best people swiftly and consistently. Our goal is to connect our candidates with our clients who have a similar goal of improving the healthcare organizations and communities they serve.



We believe that strong and transparent communication creates an efficient and composed search and is an indispensable ingredient for success. Our pillars of service are accessibility and responsiveness \- know that we can be reached in times of crisis, celebration, or just to reconnect; we are 24/7 partners not just to our clients but to our candidate partners. We provide concierge\-level service throughout each executive and director\-level search we conduct.

CHIEF OPERATIONS OFFICER \|GANA\-A'YOO, LIMITED



JOB OVERVIEW



The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is responsible for the oversight and management of the daily operations of the Corporation and its subsidiaries, with a focus on federal contracting activities. The COO ensures operational excellence, regulatory compliance, and profitability across business lines while aligning activities with the Corporation's mission, values, and Alaska Native Shareholder interests. This role serves as a strategic partner to the CEO, Board of Directors, and subsidiary leadership teams.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


**Strategic Leadership**


* Partner with the CEO to develop and execute strategic initiatives that support sustainable growth and shareholder value.
* Translate corporate goals into actionable operational plans across subsidiaries and divisions.
* Foster collaboration between corporate and subsidiary leadership to ensure alignment and synergy.
* Support and promote the cultural values and long\-term vision of the Alaska Native Village Corporation.


**Operational Oversight**


* Oversee day\-to\-day operations of the Corporation and subsidiaries engaged in federal contracting under SBA 8(a), HUBZone, or other socioeconomic programs.
* Ensure subsidiaries maintain compliance with SBA, FAR, DFARS, and other federal regulations.
* Implement operational policies, internal controls, and management systems to ensure effective contract delivery and performance.
* Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) and financial metrics to assess operational effectiveness and profitability.


**Federal Contracting \& Compliance**


* Oversee proposal development, pricing strategy, and contract execution for federal projects.
* Partner with General Counsel to ensure compliance with SBA 8(a) regulations, size standards, and affiliation rules.
* Coordinate with General Counsel and Compliance teams to maintain corporate certifications, licenses, and registrations (SAM.gov, SBA, DCAA, etc.).
* Develop risk management frameworks to address performance, audit, and compliance risks.


**Financial Management**


* Work with CFO to align operating budgets with strategic goals.
* Drive cost efficiency and financial accountability across subsidiaries.
* Support the evaluation of new investments, acquisitions, and joint ventures.
* Contribute to annual planning, forecasting, and reporting processes.


**Leadership \& Culture**


* Mentor and develop subsidiary General Managers and operational leaders.
* Promote a culture of ethical business practices, shareholder value, and respect for Alaska Native heritage.
* Encourage professional development, performance management, and succession planning.
* Lead by example in maintaining transparency, collaboration, and accountability.


QUALIFICATIONS


**Education \& Experience**


* Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Management, Finance, or a related field required; MBA or equivalent preferred.
* Minimum of 10 years of progressive leadership experience, including at least 5 years in executive management within a federal contracting environment.
* Experience with SBA 8(a) program operations, government contracting (FAR/DFARS), and Alaska Native or Tribal corporation management strongly preferred.
* Proven record of managing multi\-subsidiary operations, project performance, and organizational growth.


**Preferred Qualifications**


* Experience working with or within an Alaska Native Corporation or other Native entity.
* Knowledge of SBA 8(a) compliance, DCAA audits, and GSA contracting vehicles.
* PMP or other project management certification is a plus.


**Skills \& Competencies**


* In\-depth understanding of federal procurement, contract management, and compliance frameworks.
* Strong financial acumen and analytical capability.
* Excellent leadership, communication, and relationship\-building skills.
* Strategic thinker with operational execution strength.
* Deep appreciation for Alaska Native culture, values, and corporate responsibilities to shareholders.

OUR COMMITMENT TO YOU



At GYL, we empower our employees in their careers. When you work with us, we will encourage you to follow your passions, and we promise to be committed to your safety, well\-being, and professional development.


We treat our team members well – because it's the right thing to do, and because it makes good business sense. At GYL, you will contribute to our mission, making a difference in the lives of our Alaska Native shareholder community. We work with our clients to develop creative solutions with an emphasis on our respect for our land, culture, language, tradition, and one another.


WORK ENVIRONMENT


* Primarily office\-based with periodic travel to subsidiary locations, project sites, and remote Alaska communities.
* Must be able to work flexible hours to accommodate multiple time zone operations and federal client schedules.


PHYSICAL DEMANDS



SEDENTARY WORK



The position involves predominantly sedentary work. Most tasks will be performed while sitting at a desk or a computer workstation.

Extensive use of computer screens and keyboards is required. The role involves working in various software applications and may require extended periods of screen time.

jobs.title: Director of Grants and Development
jobs.description:
**ABOUT TRENTON HEALTH TEAM**
Trenton Health Team (THT) fosters cross\-sector collaboration and implements innovative projects to improve health and well\-being in the greater Trenton community. Founded in 2006 as an effort to address healthcare delivery and utilization among partners including St. Francis Medical Center, Capital Health, Henry J. Austin Health Center, and the City of Trenton Department of Health and Human Services, THT is now one of four State\-designated Regional Health Hubs focused on addressing the social determinants of health and achieving equitable health outcomes  

THT operates with a broad understanding of what health, health equity, and well\-being mean for the Trenton region. Our work shifts in response to the needs of our community and of our partners, and is based on robust data analysis. Current priorities include chronic disease management, care management for community members with complex health needs, food and housing security, maternal and child health, mental health and substance use disorder, disability services, and neighborhood revitalization. Work in these areas is carried out with a wide range of stakeholders from across the region and across sectors, including those from the more than 100 organizations that participate in our Community Advisory Board. **POSITION OVERVIEW**
Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Director of Grants and Development will work across project teams to understand and provide input into strategic decisions about organizational priorities and funding needs. The Director will be responsible for identifying and coordinating responses to funding opportunities for Trenton Health Team priorities and projects, as well as identifying and sharing opportunities and supporting applications for funding relevant to the priorities and projects of Community Advisory Board participants and other partners.  

Individual contributions currently represent a small proportion of THT’s funding and we see the potential for growth. The Director will be an integral part of evaluating the viability of this new funding strategy as we explore how THT can build meaningful relationships with individuals who care about health equity. The Director will be responsible for guiding this evaluation and making recommendations for the possible development of a program to cultivate, solicit, and steward new major donor relationships.
Day\-to\-day responsibilities will include researching, identifying, developing, and coordinating responses to funding opportunities that support the work of THT and our partners; writing proposals for both unrestricted operating revenue and restricted projects; managing grant reporting requirements, including working with financial and program staff to ensure that reports are accurate and timely; cultivating and supporting individual donors, including acknowledging gifts and thanking donors; managing data systems to track grants and donations; and proactively remaining up\-to\-date about and engaged in THT’s and partners’ priorities, programs, and projects. **ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS*** Oversee and coordinate the full range of activities required to identify, prepare, submit, and manage funding proposals to federal, state, county, corporate, and private funders and donors.
* Draft and edit successful proposals for funding using clear and compelling language, and assist other staff with proposal preparation. Create and manage proposal development timelines and task lists.
* Develop, maintain, and steward private and corporate funder and donor relationships, as delegated by the COO.
* Understand THT’s institutional history and programs in order to represent its interests to funders, donors, and other stakeholders.
* Support cross\-functional program planning, development, and implementation to help THT meet its strategic objectives.
* Cultivate strong relationships with project leads, with a focus on understanding and fostering programmatic alignment and collaborative funding opportunities.
* Recommend and implement short\- and long\-range fund development plans that support THT’s values, mission, and priorities, including maintenance of a pipeline of relevant funding opportunities and evaluation of THT’s current and potential future individual giving program.
* Organize and lead go/no\-go funding opportunity decision processes.
* Support project leads in creating progress reports and assisting other staff with reporting to THT’s Board and leadership, funders and donors, and external stakeholders.
* Coordinate responses to partners’ requests for letters of support for their funding efforts.
* Provide ongoing support and training on proposal development processes to staff.
* Maintain current grant and donor records in databases, including grant tracking and reporting.
* Be an early and enthusiastic adopter of new technological data systems across the organization.
* Represent THT at informational meetings

 **ADDITIONAL FUNCTIONS*** Assume all other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

 **SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES**
The Director may be asked to have staff supervisory responsibilities. In that case, the Director will:* Carry out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization’s policies and applicable laws.
* Be responsible for interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems.

 **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS*** At least five years’ experience in successful grant writing and management from a wide range of funders for community\-based nonprofits.
* Excellent written English and oral communication skills with the ability to deliver strong and compelling presentations to diverse audiences.
* Excellent organizational skills.
* Attention to detail.
* Demonstrated proficiency with common office software tools and digital tools for the management of grants and donor relation

jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer - FOI Lakeland
jobs.description:
**JOB SUMMARY**



The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) serves as the senior executive leader of the Division and is responsible for overall operational, financial, strategic, and cultural performance. The CEO is responsible for executing organizational strategy, driving growth, ensuring operational excellence, and delivering exceptional patient experience and physician satisfaction across all division locations and service lines.



The CEO partners closely with OSM executive leadership, physicians, division leadership teams, and key stakeholders to ensure alignment with enterprise goals while maintaining accountability for divisional performance. The CEO serves as the primary leader for the Division, incorporating OSM's vision, mission, values, and strategic priorities into the division’s measurable results. This position serves as an exemplary role model for both staff and patients through professionalism, integrity, accountability, compassion, respect, excellence, and service.


**Strategic Leadership**
