jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
**Dupont Hospital** is a 131\-bed acute care hospital designed by physicians with patient\-centric care and experience in mind. Accredited by The Joint Commission and part of **Lutheran Health Network**, Dupont Hospital provides a wide range of medical and surgical services, including cardiology, women's, orthopedics, diagnostic imaging and emergency care. As a certified Level III Obstetric and Level III Neonatal Care Center, Dupont was among the first ten facilities in Indiana recognized as a Perinatal Center by the Indiana Department of Health. Today, it serves over 100,000 patients annually across Northern Allen County and the surrounding communities.

**Job Summary**  

  

The **Chief Operating Officer (COO)** is responsible for the overall operational management and strategic execution of non\-nursing departments within the hospital. This role oversees key business functions including patient throughput, service line development, resource utilization, operational efficiency, and revenue growth. The COO collaborates with the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Chief Financial Officer (CFO), and other senior leaders to ensure financial sustainability, regulatory compliance, and exceptional patient care outcomes. This position is also designed to develop future executive leaders, with the expectation of preparing for a potential promotion to a Chief Executive Officer role at another location. **As part of the CEO Development Program, this position will require relocation within an acceptable timeframe for promotion/transfer.**  

  

**Essential Functions**

* Provides operational oversight of assigned non\-nursing departments, ensuring high\-quality service delivery, efficiency, and cost\-effectiveness.
* Collaborates with the CEO and CFO to develop, monitor, and manage strategic business plans and financial goals, including revenue growth and expense control.
* Drives process improvement initiatives that enhance patient throughput, resource utilization, and operational outcomes.
* Partners with the CEO to identify opportunities for business development, service line expansion, and physician recruitment aligned with community needs.
* Supports medical staff relationships by addressing operational concerns, facilitating communication, and strengthening physician engagement.
* Reviews department\-level performance metrics and collaborates with managers on corrective action plans and ongoing improvement.
* Coaches and mentors department leaders to build leadership capacity, identify development opportunities, and share operational best practices.
* Contributes to budgeting and capital planning, ensuring resources are allocated effectively to support strategic priorities.
* Ensures operations comply with internal policies, external regulations, and accreditation standards.
* Participates in executive leadership meetings, strategic planning activities, and board presentations as requested.
* Performs other duties as assigned.
* Maintains regular and reliable attendance.
* Complies with all policies and standards.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's Degree in Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, or related field required
* Master's Degree in Business Administration (MBA), Healthcare Administration (MHA), or related field preferred
* 7\-9 years of progressive healthcare leadership experience, including 3–5 years in operational or executive\-level management roles with responsibility for multiple departments or service lines required
* Prior experience overseeing multiple hospital departments or service lines preferred

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

* Strong executive leadership and strategic planning skills, with the ability to drive operational performance and lead cross\-functional initiatives.
* Advanced knowledge of hospital operations, including finance, facilities, ancillary services, and regulatory compliance.
* Exceptional business acumen, including the ability to interpret financial statements, drive cost control strategies, and support revenue growth.
* Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build credibility with physicians, department leaders, and external stakeholders.
* Demonstrated ability to develop, coach, and retain high\-performing teams, fostering accountability and continuous improvement.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer, Federal Servicing
jobs.description:
MOHELA has an amazing opportunity available to the right candidate to help lead and guide our strategic plan as our next Chief Operating Officer, Federal Servicing. This is an opportunity to join our senior leadership team and a growing workforce of almost 2,000 employees. We have been voted as a top\-rated workplace by USA Today and we are seeking a dynamic leader to join our team. We are looking for someone with a track record of proven success in a senior leadership role preferably in the student loan industry. This individual must be a problem solver and work with a sense of urgency in our people\-oriented culture.


**Position Overview:**



The Chief Operating Officer is responsible for strategic and operational management of federal contract service levels, financial performance, and daily operations to ensure service requirements are consistently achieved. Develop strong partnerships with key customer staff, regulators, and stakeholders to promote trust and proactive conflict resolution. The COO leads a team of experienced professionals to be productive and efficient focusing on organizational effectiveness, development, change management, and employee engagement to strengthen employee commitment to their work, mission, and goals. The COO works closely with MOHELA's CEO and executive team to develop and implement business strategies to drive growth, profitability, and customer satisfaction.





Key Responsibilities:


* Develop strategic objectives for MOHELA Federal priorities with timelines and measurable goals, outputs, and outcomes.


* Develop and implement operational policies and procedures that align with MOHELA's overall strategic goals, objectives, and values.


* Deploy and promote specific and effective policies and practices to strengthen customer relations and focus employees on achieving the customer's mission and goals.


* Effectively partner with federal, state, and local entities to respond to audit and servicing inquiries in collaboration with MOHELA's Legal, Information Technology, Compliance, and Government Relations departments.


* Ensure compliance with all federal, state, and local laws and regulations related to student loan servicing.


* Manage and oversee the work of various operational departments, including contact centers, loan servicing, and federal financial processing.
* Develop and maintain relationships with key stakeholders, including Board Members, customers, education, and government business partners and regulators.


* Develop and implement risk management strategies to mitigate operational risks.


* Monitor and analyze key performance statistics to identify trends and areas for improvement.


* Ensure that all operational activities are carried out efficiently, effectively, and in a timely manner.


* Manage the budget and resources allocated to the operational departments to ensure that they are used effectively and efficiently.


* Develop and maintain a positive and productive highly inclusive work environment that fosters teamwork, collaboration, continuous improvement and ensures team members can thrive and that organizational goals are met.


* Provide regular reports to the CEO and other members of the executive team on the status of operational activities, key performance statistics, and other relevant metrics.


* Ensure employee performance plans are aligned with the MOHELA mission, goals, and strategic objectives, that employees receive constructive feedback, and that employees are realistically appraised and held accountable against performance standards that are clearly defined and communicated. Seek and consider employee input.
* Promote transparency in decision\-making, processes, and outcomes.
* Leverage technological resources to develop open, common, and integrated systems that enhance processes, increase productivity, improve quality, and result in successful decision\-making for federal services.
* Assess, analyze, and acquire resources in a manner that fulfills fiduciary responsibility, protects privacy, upholds cybersecurity, reduces administrative costs, and facilitates improved service for federal services.

**Minimum Requirements:**


* Must live in Missouri and/or be willing to travel 30\-40% of the time to our headquarters in Chesterfield.
* Bachelor's degree in business administration, management, finance, or a related field. A master's degree is preferred.
* 10\+ years of experience in a senior management role, preferably in student loan servicing or banking.
* Demonstrated experience in developing and implementing compliant operational policies and procedures that drive growth and profitability.
* This position requires (6C) personnel security screening in accordance with the U.S. Department of Education's (ED) policy regarding the personnel security screening requirements for all contractor and subcontractor employees. A qualified applicant must successfully submit for personnel security screening within 14 calendar days from employment offer.
* Strong knowledge of federal and state laws and regulations related to student loan servicing.
* Ability to develop and maintain positive relationships with key stakeholders, industry leaders, including federal employees serving the customer, regulators, internal stakeholders, and State of Missouri officials.
* Strong financial acumen including successful experience budgeting operations and personnel.
* Strategic planning and problem\-solving skills.
* Excellent communication, interpersonal, and leadership skills.
* Proven track record of managing and leading high\-performing teams.
* Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities in a fast\-paced environment.
* Experience in budgeting, forecasting, and financial analysis.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
**Executive Director**
======================

**Summary of the Role**
-----------------------


The Executive Director (ED) is responsible for leading, understanding, and overseeing OPPO's growing Utah operations. The Executive Director ensures the leadership team is supported in executing the organization's strategic vision while leading by example and embodying OPPO's mission of creating safe, happy, and healthy OPPOrtunities for clients and employees.


The Executive Director is responsible for ensuring financial discipline, operational excellence, regulatory compliance, organizational culture, and the highest level of care for our clients. This role provides strategic leadership, develops and mentors the management team, and drives sustainable organizational growth. The ideal Executive Director is committed to making OPPO their long\-term professional home while building a lasting legacy alongside the organization's continued success.


The Executive Director reports directly to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO).

**Prerequisites**
-----------------

* Contract experience working with DSPD and/or DHHS.
* Contract experience working with Workforce Services regarding Vocational Rehabilitation.
* Experience with organic business growth and business development.
* Strong organizational and strategic planning skills.
* Exceptional leadership and interpersonal skills with the ability to build upon a strong organizational culture.
* Demonstrated record of meeting or exceeding performance expectations.
* Bachelor's Degree required (MBA or comparable executive\-level experience preferred, but not required).
* Minimum of five (5\) years of senior leadership experience (administration and HCBS experience preferred).
* Mastery of, or ability to quickly master, Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, email, and other computer\-based applications.
* Ability to adapt, prioritize, plan strategically, and effectively delegate.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* Professional executive presence.
* Humility and a collaborative leadership style.

**Expectations**
----------------

* Oversee OPPO's DSPD contract with the State of Utah.
* Oversee Workforce Services contracts with the State of Utah.
* Ensure compliance with all applicable local, state, and federal regulations.
* Oversee Quality Assurance and Quality Improvement initiatives.
* Review and respond appropriately to Incident Reports.
* Achieve or exceed annual organizational growth targets, including a minimum of 20% growth in revenue and Net Operating Income (NOI).
* Lead people, improve systems and processes, and implement practical solutions in a respectful, collaborative, and positive manner.
* Recruit, mentor, develop, and support a high\-performing leadership team.
* Serve as the organization's primary operational problem solver.
* Prepare and submit a monthly Executive Director Report to the CEO by the 10th of each month.
* Demonstrate the flexibility to perform any role necessary to support the organization, its employees, and its clients.
* Maintain consistent communication with internal and external stakeholders to strengthen organizational relationships.
* Respond appropriately to emergencies, including those occurring during evenings, weekends, and holidays.
* Ensure the organization maintains exceptional client care, employee engagement, operational efficiency, and financial sustainability.

**Competitive Pay \& Benefits**
-------------------------------

* Paid Time Off (PTO)
* Paid Maternity/Partner Leave
* Holiday Pay
* Mileage Reimbursement Program
* Medical, Dental, Vision, Health Savings Account (HSA), and Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
* Performance Bonus tied to Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

**Other Requirements**
----------------------

* Ability to travel up to 25%.
* Ability to sit, stand, and walk for extended periods.
* Occasionally lift up to 25 pounds.

**About OPPO**
--------------


OPPO provides home and community\-based services, including employment services, to individuals with disabilities throughout Utah, Colorado and Arizona. Our team of more than 150 dedicated employees is committed to creating meaningful OPPOrtunities that empower the people we serve.


Our vision is to create safe, happy, and healthy OPPOrtunities for our clients, employees, and communities by delivering exceptional services through compassionate leadership, innovation, and operational excellence.

jobs.title: Deputy Director of Global Clinical Services
jobs.description:
The Center for Victims of Torture works toward a future in which torture ceases to exist and its victims have hope for a new life. We are an international nonprofit dedicated to healing survivors of torture. We offer rehabilitation services to those who have been tortured, train partners around the world who can prevent and treat torture, and advocate for human rights and an end to torture. We are headquartered in Minnesota, and we have US offices in Georgia and DC, as well as offices in Africa, the Middle East, and Mexico.
  
  

The Center for Victims of Torture is hiring a Deputy Director of Global Clinical Services to provide operational leadership to translate clinical strategy into coordinated high\-quality program delivery across CVT’s global portfolio of mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), physiotherapy, case management, and related services. As a key partner to the Senior Director of Global Clinical Services, this role bridges clinical vision and program operations, bringing together program management and clinical perspectives to ensure programs have the systems, resources, and support needed to deliver services with fidelity, consistency, and quality. The Deputy Director contributes an operational lens to departmental strategy development and oversees cross\-program systems including resource allocation, risk management, and coordination. This position fosters collaboration across departments and partnerships and contributes to fundraising and donor engagement by aligning program implementation with donor priorities and funding strategies.

* Candidates located in the U.S. who are authorized to work in U.S. and will not need CVT to sponsor them on a work visa.
* Candidates located in Ethiopia, Jordan, Kenya or Uganda who are authorized to work in the country in which they are located.


**Remote status:**  

* Position is fully remote.


**Benefits:**  

* Employees in benefit eligible positions are offered a competitive benefits package which includes paid time off and options for health, dental, vision, a 403(b) retirement plan, as well as employer paid life insurance, short\- and long\-term disability.
* Employees located outside of the USA are offered a benefits package that is competitive for the country where they reside.

Translate clinical strategy and vision into concrete systems, operational processes, and actionable work plans. Coordinate clinical operations across the global portfolio, ensuring consistent implementation of standards, protocols, and fidelity to priority models of care. With senior clinical leaders, identify roadblocks and implement operational solutions to strengthen clinical quality and impact. Oversee departmental budget and determine allocation of resources, with the Senior Director. Support effective and efficient use of financial, human, and operational resources across the portfolio. Establish and maintain mechanisms that promote coordination, shared decision\-making, learning exchange, and integrated programming across operational and clinical staff within the Global Clinical Services department, and with other departments, including Justice, Accountability, and Systems Change (JAS) and Evaluation and Research (E\&R).

Foster strong team cohesion and a culture of accountability, collaboration, wellbeing, and continuous improvement among staff. With the Senior Director of Global Clinical Services and Human Resources colleagues, support development and implementation of an internal organizational staff wellbeing approach and accountability framework, including integration of trauma\-informed leadership approaches.
* Program Quality, Standards and Risk Management: Provide oversight of program performance across the Global Clinical Services portfolio, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and clinical standards. Contribute to developing and maintaining systems that support the consistent adaptation and implementation of clinical approaches, and associated monitoring and evaluation processes, to promote quality, fidelity, and continuous improvement across programs, in coordination with the Evaluation and Research department. Identify operational risks and lead risk mitigation efforts related to clinical programming. Provide oversight and direction for knowledge management systems that make clinical materials, tools, and guidance accessible across programs, in partnership with the Coordination and Operations Lead.
* Partnerships and External Engagement: Build and maintain partnerships with stakeholders, peer organizations, networks, and coalitions that strengthen clinical programming, enhance coordination, expand funding opportunites, and increase collective impact. With other senior leaders, contribute to design and implementation of survivor/advocate engagement strategies, including support for survivor and community advisory mechanisms across settings. jobs.description:
The Mississippi Arts \+ Entertainment Experience (The MAX) seeks a dynamic, relationship\-driven fundraising leader to serve as its primary development professional.


Reporting to the President \+ CEO, this individual will lead all philanthropic efforts, expand contributed revenue, strengthen fundraising infrastructure, and help position the organization for future campaign success.


The MAX is entering an exciting period of growth, with plans to increase annual income by approximately $1\.5 million in new contributed revenue over the next three years. This position offers a unique opportunity to shape the future of one of Mississippi's premier cultural institutions.

**Fundraising Strategy \& Execution**

jobs.title: Director of Development & Communications- Immunology and Immunotherapy
jobs.description:
The Icahn Genomics Institute and the Mount Sinai Center for Autoimmunity seek a Director of Communication and Strategic Advancement to lead communications, visibility, and strategic advancement across major Mount Sinai initiatives spanning genomics, autoimmunity, cancer, and immunotherapy. Together, these programs bring together genomics, immunology, cancer biology, data science, human disease biology, translational research, clinical partnerships, and therapeutic innovation to advance precision approaches to immune\-mediated, malignant, and complex human disease.

  

This is a high\-impact, institution\-facing role for an energetic scientific communicator who can help define a clear public voice, media presence, donor narrative, and strategic platform for these interconnected areas. The Director will work closely with institute and center leadership, Mount Sinai faculty, institutional communications, development teams, clinical partners, and external stakeholders to communicate scientific and clinical impact across Mount Sinai and beyond.

  

The ideal candidate is a strategic thinker, exceptional writer, and proactive builder who can translate complex biomedical research into compelling narratives for academic, philanthropic, media, policy, industry, patient, and public audiences.


Strategic Communications and Mount Sinai Visibility

* Develop and execute a cohesive communications strategy that advances the reputation and identity of the Icahn Genomics Institute, the Mount Sinai Center for Autoimmunity, and aligned efforts in cancer and immunotherapy. Shape core messaging for websites, reports, proposals, presentations, press materials, donor communications, and social media. Partner with Mount Sinai communications teams to identify media opportunities, draft press materials, develop faculty profiles, and position leadership as trusted voices in genomics, immunology, autoimmunity, cancer, immunotherapy, precision medicine, translational research, and therapeutic innovation.

  

Thought Leadership and Opportunity Building

* Proactively identify opportunities to elevate these programs through media stories, perspective articles, commentaries, op\-eds, scientific meetings, donor briefings, institutional announcements, awards, partnerships, and public engagement. Help position genomics, immunology, autoimmunity, cancer, and immunotherapy as defining strengths of Mount Sinai and major frontiers for understanding, treating, and preventing human disease.

  

Grants, Initiatives, and Strategic Proposals

* Lead or substantially contribute to the writing and development of large grants, center and institute proposals, philanthropic proposals, multi\-investigator initiatives, and institutional strategic documents. Translate scientific vision, clinical relevance, program structure, milestones, deliverables, and institutional impact into clear and persuasive narratives. Draft executive summaries, specific aims, vision statements, letters of support, concept notes, donor\-facing materials, and launch documents.

  

Presentation and Advancement Materials

* Create high\-quality materials for institute and center leadership, Mount Sinai leaders, donors, advisory boards, industry partners, and external audiences. Develop pitch decks, scientific overview slides, donor presentations, annual reports, briefing documents, strategic roadmaps, website language, media pitches, and social media campaigns. Maintain a library of core slides, graphics, talking points, impact metrics, and program assets for rapid use in meetings, proposals, and external engagements.

  

Philanthropy, External Engagement, and Communications Infrastructure

* Partner with Mount Sinai development teams to articulate each program’s vision, priorities, funding needs, and patient impact for donors, foundations, and philanthropic stakeholders. Build systems to capture publications, discoveries, clinical advances, faculty achievements, funding milestones, trainee successes, technology capabilities, partnerships, and patient impact stories so these programs can communicate their value quickly and consistently.

  

Qualifications and Attributes

* The ideal candidate will have strong experience in scientific, medical, or academic communications; excellent writing and editing skills; and the ability to communicate complex biomedical ideas clearly to multiple audiences. Experience with large grants, strategic proposals, philanthropic materials, media strategy, social media, and presentation development is strongly preferred. Familiarity with genomics, immunology, oncology, autoimmunity, immunotherapy, or precision medicine is highly desirable.
* The successful candidate should be entrepreneurial, self\-directed, highly organized, and comfortable building new programs within a fast\-moving academic medical center. They should bring energy, urgency, follow\-through, strong editorial judgment, and the ability to work closely with senior faculty, institutional leaders, communications teams, development officers, clinicians, scientists, donors, and external partners.

jobs.title: Program Director (RN) - Hospice
jobs.description:
Overview:
**Crescent Hospice is looking for a Program Director to oversee our Hospice Program in Aiken! The Hospice Director will provide overall leadership for their hospice agency operations, with a focus on growth, external market relationships, financial management, customer service and quality care delivery.**  

As the Hospice Program Director, you will take on a dynamic role in overseeing and administering all aspects of our day\-to\-day operations. You will work closely with established goals, objectives, policies, and regulations of our esteemed company. Your responsibilities will include ensuring compliance with all hospice\-specific regulations, laws, and policies, including those related to Medicare/Medicaid matters. Under the guidance of senior management, you will expertly manage the affairs of our local office, making a significant impact on the lives of patients and their families during difficult times. **Who we are:**
At Crescent Hospice, we take immense pride in being a mission\-driven, patient\-centered leader in end\-of\-life care. Guided by our vision to be the most trusted partner in hospice care, we surround our patients and their loved ones with unwavering support, comfort, and compassion. At Crescent, we look for dedicated professionals who share our belief that true hospice care extends beyond medical needs—it’s about bringing dignity, peace, and human connection to every life we touch. **We offer a supportive, growth\-oriented environment along with a comprehensive benefits package that includes:*** ***Comprehensive Health, Dental, \& Vision Insurance***
* ***Career Path Program that supports internal growth, advancement, and increased pay***
* ***A generous time\-off package with 15 days of PTO \& 10 Holidays to rest and recharge***
* ***Tuition Reimbursement \& Certification Assistance to support your professional growth***
* ***Wellness \& Discount Programs to help you lead a healthy and balanced life***
* ***Cell Phone, Mileage, \& Gym Membership Reimbursement for your convenience***
* ***Company matching 401(k) to secure your future***
* ***Hands\-on Clinical Onboarding Program to ensure you have a smooth transition into our team***


Responsibilities:
* **Forge Strong Connections:** Partner with our Liaisons to foster good working relations with physicians, hospitals, nursing facilities, and more. Together, we'll extend our reach and help even more people!
* **Build the Dream Team:** Employ qualified colleagues and ensure adequate colleague orientation, training, education, and evaluation. Together, we'll grow and thrive!
* **Be the Backbone of Excellence:** Organize and supervise the administrative functions of the hospice program and overall local operations. Your skills will keep us running smoothly!
* **Compliance Champion:** Maintain compliance with applicable laws and regulations and implement corrective action if needed. Your attention to detail will keep us on the right track!
* **Lead with Purpose:** Take charge of the day\-to\-day management and operations of the hospice program. Your leadership will drive us toward success!
* **Policy Implementer:** Make a difference by implementing the policies and procedures approved by the governing body. Your commitment will shape our future!


Qualifications:
* Bachelor's degree in nursing, health care, or business administration preferred.
* Minimum of two (2\) years' experience in health care management, home health, hospice, or related health programs required.
* Two (2\) years of hospice experience required with intimate knowledge of Medicare/Medicaid and Department of Aging and Disability Services regulations.
* Operations and/or Sales Leadership experience required
* Demonstrated ability to develop and maintain relationships in the communities served as well as within a company.
* Skilled at establishing/maintaining working relationships with key staff, marketing contacts, and clinical staff to ensure the thorough understanding of Hospice Mission and services.
* Experience in analyzing processes, improvement planning, supporting change, and effectively managing priorities in a fast\-paced environment.

**$110,000 \- $115,000 per year (Average Pay Range). The pay range listed represents a general guideline for the role and is not a guarantee of the final offer. Compensation will be determined based on the selected candidate’s relevant experience and the specific responsibilities of the position. Final compensation rate will be discussed and confirmed at the conclusion of the interview process.**

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
**JExecutive Director**

**Greater Lake Placid Chamber of Commerce**  
**Lake Placid, Florida**

**Job Type**

Full\-time

**Salary**

*Competitive salary based on qualifications and experience.*

**Position Summary**

The Greater Lake Placid Chamber of Commerce is seeking a dynamic, community\-minded Executive Director to lead the organization in fulfilling its mission of promoting local business, tourism, and economic vitality while enhancing the quality of life in the Greater Lake Placid area.

The Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of the Chamber and reports directly to the Board of Directors. This individual is responsible for strategic leadership, financial management, membership growth and retention, event oversight, tourism promotion, staff supervision, and fostering strong relationships with businesses, government agencies, community organizations, and volunteers.

The ideal candidate is an energetic leader with strong business acumen, exceptional communication skills, and a passion for community development.

**Essential Responsibilities**

**Leadership \& Administration**

* Provide overall leadership and daily management of Chamber operations.
* Develop and implement strategic goals established by the Board of Directors.
* Advise and collaborate with the Board on organizational priorities.
* Supervise, and evaluate Chamber staff and volunteers.
* Ensure compliance with all Chamber policies and applicable regulations.

**Financial Management**

* manage the annual operating budget.
* Monitor revenues and expenditures.
* Oversee financial reporting and work with the Bookkeeper and Board to ensure fiscal responsibility.
* Seek new revenue opportunities through sponsorships, grants, memberships, and fundraising initiatives.

**Membership Development**

* Recruit new Chamber members.
* Retain existing members through excellent service and engagement.
* Promote the benefits and value of Chamber membership.
* Develop programs that increase member participation and satisfaction.

**Community Relations**

* Serve as the public face of the Chamber.
* Build and maintain positive relationships with local businesses, elected officials, civic organizations, tourism partners, and community stakeholders.
* Represent the Chamber at community meetings, events, and public functions.

**Marketing \& Communications**

* Oversee Chamber marketing efforts including social media, website, newsletters, visitor information, and public relations.
* Promote Chamber programs, events, and member businesses.
* Enhance the Chamber's visibility throughout the region.

**Event Management**

* Provide leadership and oversight for Chamber\-sponsored events including festivals, networking events, educational programs, and fundraising activities.
* Coordinate with committees, volunteers, sponsors, and vendors to ensure successful event execution.

**Tourism \& Visitor Services**

* Support tourism initiatives that promote Lake Placid as a destination.
* Oversee visitor services and community information provided by the Chamber.

**Qualifications**

* Minimum of 3\-5 years of progressively responsible leadership or management experience.
* Experience managing budgets and financial operations.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills.
* Demonstrated ability to build relationships with diverse stakeholders.
* Excellent organizational and project management skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and common office technology.
* Chamber of Commerce or association management experience.
* Nonprofit leadership experience.
* Experience with fundraising and sponsorship development.
* Event planning and management experience.
* Marketing and social media experience.
* Grant writing or grant administration experience.

**Knowledge, Skills \& Abilities**

* Leadership and team development
* Public speaking and presentation skills
* Financial management
* Membership recruitment and retention
* Conflict resolution
* Community engagement
* Event planning
* Marketing and public relations
* Time management
* Problem solving
* Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with the Board of Directors

**Work Environment**

* Primarily office\-based with regular attendance at community meetings and Chamber events.
* Some evening and weekend work required.
* Occasional lifting of event materials up to 30 pounds.
* Valid Florida driver's license and reliable transportation preferred.

**Benefits**

* Paid holidays
* Paid vacation
* Professional development opportunities
* Opportunity to make a meaningful impact in the Lake Placid community

Submit your resume and cover letter, identifying the position you are applying for in the subject line to:

**information@lpfla.com**

**Executive Director Job Description**

**San Luis Obispo County Arts Council**

August 3, 2026

**Position Overview**

The Executive Director provides strategic leadership and operational management for the

San Luis Obispo County Arts Council. Reporting to the Board of Directors, with day to day

contact through the Board President, the Executive Director is responsible for advancing the

organization's mission, overseeing programs and staff, ensuring the organization's fiscal

health, leading fundraising, and serving as the primary public voice of the organization.

**Leadership and Governance**

Provide overall leadership and direction consistent with the organization's mission and

strategic priorities. Partner with the Board of Directors on governance, planning, and

organizational development. Operate within the board approval and escalation matrix set

out in the Board/Executive Director Authority and Communication Framework.

Fiscal Management and Accountability

Develop and manage the annual budget for board approval. Maintain accurate, timely

financial records and reporting. Meet with the treasurer on a consistent cadence to review

budget performance and resolve discrepancies.

Ensure compliance with grant, contract, and regulatory financial requirements. Read,

interpret, and act independently on financial statements and reports. Flag financial concerns

to the board promptly, consistent with the Authority and Communication Framework.

**Fundraising and Development**

Lead fundraising efforts, including grant writing, donor cultivation, and individual and

corporate giving. Maintain a consistent, weekly cadence of in person meetings with

prospective and current donors.

Represent the organization at community and arts events as a channel for donor cultivation

and relationship building. Meet fundraising targets established annually with the board.

Maintain accurate donor records and ensure timely acknowledgment and reporting.

**Program Management**

Oversee the design, implementation, and evaluation of the organization's programs,

including grant funded initiatives. Ensure programs are administered consistently with

donor agreements, grant terms, and board approved guidelines. Administer programs such

as Open Studios Art Tour

**Communication**

Serve as the primary point of contact between staff, the board, and the community.

Communicate proactively and promptly on emerging issues, risks, and matters likely to

require board action, consistent with the Authority and Communication Framework. Provide

regular written updates to the Board President and board.

**Community Engagement and Advocacy**

Represent the organization to donors, partners, government entities, and the public. Attend

County Board of Supervisors meetings and other relevant meetings of elected officials on a

regular basis, providing public comment on arts related matters as appropriate. Convene or

participate in regular meetings of arts organization leaders countywide to coordinate on

shared issues, funding opportunities, and advocacy priorities. Build and maintain

relationships with tourism boards, chambers of commerce, and other regional partners.

Advocate for the arts across the county at the local, regional, and state level.

**Staff and Contractor Management**

Hire, supervise, and support staff and contractors. Set clear expectations and provide regular

feedback to staff, including a documented annual review for each staff member.

Evaluate contractor work against the terms of each agreement. Ensure contractor

classification and agreements comply with applicable state and federal labor law. Maintain

accurate role descriptions and workload allocation across programs.

**Qualifications**

● Non\-profit or equivalent leadership experience, with a demonstrated track record of

successful fundraising, including direct donor cultivation and solicitation.

● Working knowledge of nonprofit financial management sufficient to read, interpret, and

act independently on financial statements and budgets.

● Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience representing an

organization to the public, media, and government bodies.

● Demonstrated ability to manage staff and contractors effectively.

● Commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion.

● Existing knowledge of, or ties to, San Luis Obispo County's arts, philanthropic, or civic

community preferred.

Work Location: In person

new_jobs.description:
**Managing Director, Business Development, National Corporate Partnerships** ***(Full\-time)***

**POSITION REPORTS TO**: Jerry Ochoa, Vice President, National Corporate Partnerships

**PRIORITY APPLICATION DEADLINE**: Friday, August 14th. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis after this deadline.

**LOCATION**: Flexible

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**
------------------


We are looking for a Managing Director, Business Development to lead Teach For America's pursuit of new national corporate partnerships and to build the next generation of corporate partnerships that fund Teach For America's mission. In this role, you will set the vision, strategy, and pipeline that fuel our corporate business development engine, and you will personally lead the cultivation and closing of six\- and seven\-figure new corporate partnerships that advance TFA's mission.


The ideal candidate will be energized by the blank\-page work of business development. You find where TFA's mission intersects a company's priorities, design partnership models that don't yet exist, and build the case that moves a prospect from cold to closed. You are at ease with senior corporate leaders, from C\-suite executives to heads of CSR and corporate foundations, and you translate those relationships into meaningful, mission\-aligned investments. You bring a sharp strategic mind, deep fluency in the corporate philanthropy landscape, and a proven track record of closing new business at scale. You will be equally comfortable in the boardroom and in the weeds of a prospect pipeline. You bring curiosity and openness to how emerging technologies — particularly AI — can accelerate your work, and you approach these tools with fluency, critical thinking, and a strong ethical grounding.


The goal is to secure new, high\-value corporate partnerships that expand TFA's national revenue base and deepen our long\-term financial sustainability. For the current fiscal year, the team charge will be between $3M\-$5M in new money.

**WHAT YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR**
----------------------------------


Business Development Strategy and Vision (20%)

* Set the annual and multi\-year strategy for new corporate revenue, including national goals, target sectors, and priority prospect lists.
* Build and maintain the business development team's infrastructure, KPIs, and workflow management processes.
* Develop annual priorities and tactics that grow TFA's corporate revenue base and align to organizational fundraising goals.

new_jobs.title: Development Director
new_jobs.description:
Title: Development Director

Position Status: Full\-time, exempt

Reports to: CEO

**OPPORTUNITY**

Palo Alto Humane has spent more than a century championing the human\-animal bond — and we're at an inflection point. Our programs are growing, our community presence is deepening, and we're ready to build the fundraising infrastructure to match our ambition.

This is a rare opportunity for a fundraiser who wants to own something. You won't be inheriting a rigid system or managing a large team — you'll be the architect of our development function, with direct access to leadership, a board that's engaged and ready to open doors, and a mission that resonates deeply with donors in one of the most philanthropically active regions in the country.

If you're energized by the idea of building something that lasts — a donor community, a major gifts pipeline, a culture of philanthropy — and you want your work to have a direct, visible impact on animals and the people who love them, we'd love to meet you.

**ORGANIZATION**

Palo Alto Humane’s mission is to inspire our community to connect humanely with animals. We believe in the transformative bond between humans and animals and aim to support both. We are a 501(c)(3\) nonprofit, charitable, volunteer\-supported organization, and one of the few humane societies nationwide with no animal shelter.

Our programs and services ensure pets remain in homes with their families, support spay/neuter efforts across Santa Clara County and provide experiences for people to connect with friendly pets when they may not have a pet of their own. For more than a century PAH’s focus has been to alleviate the suffering of animals, increase public sensitivity to animal issues and elevate the status of animals in our society.

**POSITION DETAILS**

As our dedicated Development Director, you'll lead all fundraising strategy and execution — from major gifts and donor stewardship to solicitations and the Charity Checkout program. You'll report directly to the CEO and work closely with our board and small team to build PAH's development function from the ground up.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES** 

*Fundraising Strategy \& Donor Relations*

* Design and lead PAH's comprehensive fundraising strategy — spanning major gifts, annual campaigns, recurring donors, donor advised funds, planned giving, giving platforms, and written solicitations.
* Set annual and multi\-year fundraising goals and budgets in partnership with the CEO.
* Identify, cultivate and steward major donors, corporate partners, and legacy sponsors alongside the CEO.
* Oversee donor stewardship and recognition – ensuring acknowledgements, tax receipts, and creative recognition ideas reflect fundraising best practices.
* Maintain the donor database, ensuring accurate records and meaningful donor engagement.
* Develop engagement plans for stock giving and donor advised fund giving.
* Build and grow the “Charity Checkout” program, our point\-of\-sale giving initiative with local veterinary practices and businesses.

*Communications \& Marketing*

* Partner with the Director of Community Engagement (and Marketing Consultant) to create stories and content across social media, email solicitations and communications, newsletters annual reports, and press releases that bring PAH’s mission and impact to life.
* Help grow PAH’s digital presence, including our website and social channels.

*Organizational Leadership \& Reporting*

* Provide regular fundraising updates to the Board and leadership team.
* Set key performance indicators (KPIs) for fundraising and marketing efforts, using real\-time data to refine strategy. Help build a culture of philanthropy across PAH \- coaching staff, board members, and volunteers on fundraising.
* Engage in ongoing professional development and goal\-setting with the CEO.

As a small team, we all wear multiple hats — we're looking for someone who sees that as an opportunity, not a constraint.

**WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE**

In your first 90 days, you'll get to know PAH from the inside out — meeting with the CEO, board, and staff, auditing our current donor database and fundraising materials, and building relationships with our key supporters. By the end of this period, you'll have a clear picture of where we stand and draft a roadmap for the year ahead.

By the end of year one, you'll have launched at least one new fundraising initiative or strengthened an existing program (such as a robust DAF program, a major gifts pipeline, or an extensive Charity Checkout program). In addition, you will have established KPIs that give leadership and the board real visibility into fundraising performance, and built the early foundation of a donor stewardship system that will support PAH's growth for years to come.

**QUALIFICATIONS** 

* Passion for PAH’s mission, vision and core values.
* Minimum of five years of fundraising experience in the nonprofit sector, and a college degree or extensive experience in relationship management roles (private foundations, sales, financial advising, etc.).
* Proven success developing and executing fundraising initiatives.
* Experience cultivating, soliciting and stewarding individual donors.
* Exposure to major gifts work or program, or experience managing a donor portfolio desired.
* Demonstrated ability to increase revenue and ensure long\-term strategic growth.
* Self\-starter with the ability to drive projects to completion with minimal supervision.
* Strong problem\-solver and critical thinker, ability to synthesize data and make evidence\-based decisions.
* Persuasive and clear communicator with excellent organizational, written, verbal and interpersonal skills.
* Proficiency in DonorPerfect (or similar donor software platforms such as Blackbaud or Salesforce), Constant Contact, Google Workspace, Microsoft Suite, Canva, VistaPrint, and digital marketing tools.

LifeMoves is the largest and most effective provider of housing and services for neighbors experiencing homelessness in Silicon Valley since 1987\. With 40 programs, LifeMoves gives our neighbors experiencing homelessness a temporary place to call home while providing intensive, customized case management through site\-based programs and community outreach.

Join us today, and experience a career well lived.  


**Program Director, IDD Services**
**$70,304/yr**  

Have you been looking for a fantastic role to continue your career path in Social and Human Services? Look no further. This role is critical to our success and exemplifies the wonderful mission driven work we do here every day.  

  

* Manage the day\-to\-day operations of one to four programs in a community including organization and implementation of direct supports, person\-centered planning, and implementation, health care, advocacy, stakeholder relations, regulatory compliance, recruiting, retention, staffing, training, safety, financial management, and maintenance of the physical environment.
* Manage program staff members including performance evaluations, scheduling, and orientation.
* Make recommendations and/or decisions on employee hires, transfers, promotions, salary changes, corrective action, and terminations.
* Manage the implementation of program planning; monitor delivery of services and supports; ensure services are consistent, engaging, and relevant to the individuals served.
* Must be available on\-call to support staff, find coverage or cover shifts as needed.


***Qualifications:***  



* Bachelor's degree and two to three years of related experience in the Human Services Industry preferred.
* An equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Other education, experience, training, licensure, or certification per state requirements or as required by applicable regulations.
* Current driver's license, car registration, and auto insurance.
* Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and the ability to multi\-task to meet deadlines.
* Effective communication skills to manage relationships.
* A reliable, responsible attitude and a compassionate approach.


***Why Join Us?***  



* Full, Part\-time, and As Needed schedules available.
* Full compensation/benefits package for full\-time employees.
* 401(k) with company match.
* Paid time off and holiday pay.
* Rewarding work, impacting the lives of those you serve, working alongside a great team of coworkers.
* Enjoy job security with nationwide career development and advancement opportunities.


**We have a rewarding work environment with awesome co\-workers – come join our team –** ***Apply Today!***

  

Sevita is a leading provider of home and community\-based specialized health care. We believe that everyone deserves to live a full, more independent life. We provide people with quality services and individualized supports that lead to growth and independence, regardless of the physical, intellectual, or behavioral challenges they face.
  

  

We’ve made this our mission for more than 50 years. And today, our 40,000 team members continue to innovate and enhance care for the 50,000 individuals we serve all over the U.S.

new_jobs.title: Associate Executive Director
new_jobs.description:
Take the next step in your career with this rewarding opportunity to join the YMCA of South Hampton Roads.
Job Description
Under the direction of the Executive Director, the Associate Executive Director is responsible for overseeing the daily operations. This position provides cause\-driven leadership in staff supervision, volunteer management, fiscal oversight, financial development, program administration, facility and equipment stewardship, community relations, and personal and professional development.


Qualifications
* Strong business operations background with a proven track record for producing growth, annual giving and strong financial management
* A Bachelor's Degree in a child related field or Sports Management/ Recreation/Health Sciences is preferred, or 48 semester hours or 72 quarter hours of college credit of which 12 semester hours or 18 quarter hours are in subjects relating to children.
* Five or more years of successful management experience, preferably in a YMCA or other nonprofit agency in the health \& wellness, business or related field
* Supervision of full and part\-time employees and accountability for annual budget exceeding $1 million
* Ability to lead assigned operations including staff development and supervision, development and monitoring of budgets, membership and program development, financial development, marketing and public relations, board and volunteer development
* Ability to establish and maintain collaborations with community organizations
* YMCA Multi\-Team Leader certification preferred
**WORKING CONDITIONS:**

* This role requires daily onsite work and occasional after\-hours response; therefore, candidates must be able to reliably commute to the assigned location and reside within approximately 30 miles or 45 minutes of the worksite by their start date to meet operational needs
* Requires a person of maturity and good judgment, who can operate with a minimum of guidance from the Division Vice President
* Requires ability to exercise appropriate independent judgment, to assess facts and issues, and make non\-routine decisions regarding day\-to\-day operational problems and issues
* Requires effective team\-building and team\-leadership skills
* Must maintain cooperative, functional relationships with senior leadership team, peers, and subordinates
* Must maintain positive, energetic attitude toward YMCA work, goals, and values
* Must have ability to respond to emergencies 24 hours a day, and to travel as needed for operational management, including on\-site presence in managing major operational problems
* Must have superior oral and written communication skills and the ability to respond to a wide variety of constituencies, including staff, volunteers, members, program participants, vendors, community leaders, etc.
* Performs the duties of direct reports as needed

**ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS, PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:**

* Physically able to successfully complete required job functions, including use of hands, arms, fingers, able to talk and hear, use a computer, sit and stand, regularly move/lift up to 50 pounds, enter all YMCA environments (office spaces, indoor and outdoor maintenance/mechanical areas, fitness areas, pool and pool space, camping areas, unimproved outdoor locations and other program areas)
* Continuous operations requiring attention to detail and multi\-tasking
* Physically able to successfully complete required certifications
Essential Functions
**Division of Duties:**

* 65% Direct leadership of all day\-to\-day operations
* 20% \- Property Management
* 10% \- Leadership role in the Annual Impact Fund
* 5% \- Staff development of direct reports

**Priorities**

* Supervise all the day\-to\-day operations of the assigned location.
* Develop, manage, and achieve the budget expectations with an emphasis on licensed childcare programs, Events and Rentals, Sports and Aquatic programming, Community Relations, and Fundraising.
* Assist with all fundraising efforts with an emphasis on staff and community giving.
* Support board development by assisting the Executive Director in recruiting three new board members annually and leading a board subcommittee.
* Oversee property management, ensuring the upkeep of all grounds and facilities.
* Foster relationship development with key home office leaders, including VPs of various product lines.

**Budget and Financial Performance**

* Develop, manage, and monitor operating budgets to meet or exceed targets.
* Initiate adjustments to operations to ensure a balanced budget.
* Ensure completion of monthly variance reports and forecasting.

**Program Development and Membership Engagement**

* Implements Association childcare strategies that support recruitment of new participants and retention of existing participants. Creates a member\-focused culture and models relationship\-building skills in all interactions. Uses YMCA “listen first” skills to understand and respond to the needs, wants and interests of participants. Fosters a climate of innovation and resolves problems to ensure participant satisfaction
* Develops long\-range plans for the expansion of programs and services in harmony with overall YMCA objectives.
* Monitors the achievements of these objectives and exercises appropriate action to assure the achievements of the objectives are of the highest quality programs and services
* Represents and promotes the YMCA in the local community by developing positive working and collaborative relationships with other organizations, businesses, and governmental entities
* Ensures safety, cleanliness, and function of all related facilities and equipment

**Team Performance Toward Organizational Goals**

* Development and supervision of the Family Center operations
* Recruits, hires, trains, develops, and leads employees and volunteers. Reviews and evaluates staff performance.
* Develops strategies to motivate staff and achieve goals. Responsible for supervision of exempt and non exempt employees
*

**Employment Status**: Exempt, Full Time; Occasional evening/weekends required  

**Reports to:** State Executive Director  

**Location:** Hybrid (Tacoma, WA)  

**Travel:** Occasional regional travel (WA State) required  

**Pay Range:** $96,000 \- $144,000 per year  

*This represents the full pay range for the position; most new hires can expect an offer between the minimum and midpoint of the range, depending on experience.*

 **ABOUT COMMUNITIES IN SCHOOLS OF WASHINGTON**


For over 30 years, Communities In Schools of Washington (CISWA), in partnership with the 12 local network affiliates across Washington state, has been striving for equity in educational opportunities. The state office is a small, high\-energy office that has a history of strong operations and successful outcomes built upon community partnerships. Driven by our core values of collaboration, opportunity, access, and transformation and in adherence to the CIS National guidelines, the state office works to ensure that all affiliates and their Boards of Directors have the tools and capacity to provide and sustain strong student programs and services in their local communities as they work directly inside K\-12 schools supporting students who have historically been furthest from educational justice.

 **JOB SUMMARY**


The Development Director leads the CISWA State Office’s resource development strategy, creating and executing comprehensive multi\-year and annual fundraising plans to meet ambitious revenue goals. Reporting to the State Executive Director, this role manages the Development team, directly oversees fundraising for the State Office and two in\-house affiliates, leverages board member engagement, and provides consultative leadership to strengthen fundraising capacity across Washington’s CIS affiliate network. The ideal candidate brings 7\+ years of relevant nonprofit resource development expertise (equivalent combination of education and experience), a strong work ethic and drive for excellence, and a commitment to equity, collaboration, and youth\-centered practice in alignment with our organizational values.

 **KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Strategic Fundraising \& Resource Development**

* Create and implement a comprehensive fund development plan that meets the agency’s strategic and financial goals and aligns with legislative and advocacy efforts.
* Cultivate and grow corporate and foundation relationships, including event sponsorships and new avenues for support.
* Implement and optimize individual, major giving, and planned giving programs, including donor cultivation, stewardship, and friend\-raising events.
* Plan and execute fundraising events; secure sponsorships and contracted support, and collaborate with board members, staff, and volunteers to meet revenue goals.
* Serve on and collaborate with the Board Resource Development Committee to lead board fundraising efforts; coach and mentor board members to leverage their talents and connections for resource development.
* Lead and manage the Development team.
* Directly manage and support fund development for CISWA’s in\-house affiliates; provide hands\-on resource development services as part of the State Office team.
* Collaborate with the Marketing \& Communications team to align donor messaging with the agency’s communications plan, centering student voice and ethical storytelling practices.
* Pursue ongoing professional development and industry training to stay current on fundraising trends in the nonprofit and local community.

**Capacity Building for Statewide Affiliate Networ****k**

* Advise and consult with independent Washington CIS affiliate executive directors, boards, and resource development professionals to strengthen fundraising skills and capacity within their local communities.
* Develop and lead collaborative fundraising strategies through an affiliate network Resource Development committee.
* Convene affiliate resource development staff and facilitate learning communities, share best practices, and support continuous professional development.

**General Duties**

* Foster a culture of teamwork and community\-centric fundraising across the state office and affiliate network.
* Represent Washington in national CIS initiatives and partnerships.
* Maintain ethical and professional standards as a CISWA representative.
* Demonstrate leadership and partnership in alignment with the state office values and commitment to local empowerment.
* Perform other duties as assigned in a small team\-oriented nonprofit office.

**JOB QUALIFICATIONS**

**Experience \& Education**
===========================

* 7\+ years of nonprofit or community organization fundraising experience with increasing responsibility; an equivalent combination of education (nonprofit management, business, marketing, or communications) and experience will be considered.
* Proven track record of developing and implementing successful resource development plans with clearly defined fund strategies, including engaging board members in donor cultivation and gift solicitation.
* 3\+ years of supervisory or managerial experience.
* Public speaking and presentations for small to mid\-sized audiences.
* Experience with a federated organizational structure a plus.
* CFRE certification a plus.
* Experience with professional mentoring, peer learning facilitation, or leading professional development training a plus.

**Demonstrated Skills:**
========================

* Exceptional relationship\-building skills to secure donors and partners and foster teamwork.
* Strong leadership skills to motivate staff, network leaders, and board members.
* Highly collaborative and solution\-focused, with strong organizational and prioritization skills across multiple projects.
* Excellent written, oral, and public speaking/presentation skills for small to mid\-sized audiences.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and client relationship management (CRM) database software, and virtual/telework

new_jobs.description:
Hillel Academy of Pittsburgh is a growing Orthodox Jewish day school serving students from Early Childhood through Grade 12 on the Yitzy Sutofsky Campus. We provide an exceptional Orthodox Jewish and general studies education in a warm, nurturing environment that prepares students to become thoughtful, accomplished, and committed members of the Jewish community and broader society. We are seeking an experienced, creative, and mission\-driven Director of Marketing and Communications to lead the school’s strategic marketing, branding, institutional storytelling, and communications efforts. Working closely with the CEO, COO, Principal and Educational Director, and other administrators, this individual will strengthen Hillel Academy’s brand, support enrollment and fundraising, and communicate the school’s impact to families, donors, alumni, and the broader community.


STRATEGY


Lead integrated marketing and brand strategy.


STORYTELLING


Showcase the impact of a Hillel Academy education.


GROWTH


Support enrollment, fundraising, and engagement.


Key Responsibilities

* Strategic Marketing \& Brand Leadership: Develop and execute an integrated strategy aligned with the school’s


mission, strategic priorities, enrollment goals, and fundraising objectives; safeguard the Hillel Academy brand and advise senior leadership on communications.

* Enrollment \& Advancement Marketing: Create campaigns and materials that support student recruitment and retention, annual and capital fundraising, donor stewardship, alumni engagement, and major institutional initiatives.
* Institutional Storytelling \& Community Engagement: Share compelling stories about students, faculty, alumni, Jewish life, academics, athletics, arts, STEM, and community service; strengthen relationships with families, donors, community partners, and media.
* Digital, Creative \& Communications Oversight: Oversee the website, social media, email, print, video, photography, advertising, newsletters, press releases, event promotions, and branded materials; maintain consistent quality and messaging across platforms.
* Internal \& Crisis Communications: Support clear internal communications and assist senior leadership with sensitive, urgent, or crisis\-related messaging, talking points, parent notices, FAQs, and public statements.
* Analytics \& Operations: Monitor engagement and campaign performance, manage communications budgets and vendors, and create systems that keep projects accurate, efficient, and on schedule.


Qualifications

* Bachelor’s degree in marketing, communications, public relations, journalism, English, business, or a related field preferred.
* Professional experience in marketing, communications, branding, public relations, advancement communications, or a related field.
* Exceptional writing, editing, proofreading, storytelling, project management, and strategic communications skills.
* Experience with websites, email marketing, social media, print materials, multimedia content, and integrated campaigns.
* Excellent judgment, discretion, organization, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders.


Hillel Academy of Pittsburgh • Director of Marketing and Communications

* Independent school, Jewish communal, nonprofit, educational, or other mission\-driven experience strongly preferred.
* Knowledge of Orthodox Jewish practices, culture and values, Jewish day school education, and the Pittsburgh Jewish community required.


The Ideal Candidate


The successful candidate will be strategic, creative, highly organized, collaborative, responsive, and service\-oriented. This person will be comfortable balancing long\-term planning with immediate communications needs and will be passionate about Orthodox Jewish education and the impact of Hillel Academy.

new_jobs.title: Chief Development Officer
new_jobs.description:
**Chief Development Officer****About the Client** Our client is a mission\-driven nonprofit focused on civic education and democracy\-building, engaging youth and communities in civic learning nationwide. As the organization scales its impact, they're building out a modern development function to match their ambitions — creating a brand\-new C\-suite role to lead the charge.


**About the Role** This is a newly created, first\-ever Chief Development Officer position, reporting directly to the President \& CEO and overseeing a team of 2 (including a Sr. Director of Advancement). The CDO will own org\-wide development strategy, leading the transformation from a grant\-centered funding model to a diversified, relationship\-driven philanthropy operation spanning major gifts, annual giving, corporate partnerships, alumni engagement, and institutional funding. This is a hands\-on leadership role — the CDO will personally manage a portfolio of high\-capacity donors and close six\- and seven\-figure gifts, while also building the systems, team, and board engagement needed for long\-term fundraising growth.


**Responsibilities**

* Own org\-wide development strategy and drive an initial $600K–$1M in annual contributed revenue, with sustained year\-over\-year growth
* Lead the shift from grant\-centered fundraising to a diversified, relationship\-driven philanthropy model (major gifts, annual giving, corporate partnerships, alumni, institutional)
* Personally manage a portfolio of high\-capacity donors; close six\- and seven\-figure gifts; run moves management and stewardship
* Build alumni\-engagement pathways to convert former program participants into an active donor community
* Lead and mentor the development team; set KPIs, dashboards, and forecasting; ensure disciplined CRM (Salesforce) usage
* Serve as the CEO's fundraising partner and drive board engagement in donor cultivation and solicitation

**Requirements**

* 10\+ years of progressive nonprofit development/fundraising/advancement experience, including ownership of fundraising strategy and revenue growth
* Demonstrated success personally closing multiple six\- and seven\-figure gifts
* 5\+ years supervising development staff
* Proven ability to build a diversified development function beyond grants
* Genuine mission alignment with civic education, democracy, and/or youth civic learning

**Benefits \& Why Join**

* Ground\-floor opportunity to build and define a brand\-new C\-suite function
* Direct partnership with the CEO and board on organizational fundraising strategy
* Hybrid/remote flexibility, with HQ based in Calabasas, CA

new_jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
new_jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**Position Title:** Chief Operating Officer (COO)

**Reports To:** Chief Executive Officer

**Department:** Executive Leadership

**Status:** Exempt

**Date:** July 2026

 **Broad Functions:** The Chief Operating Officer (COO) provides operational and financial leadership for the company's portfolio of restaurant and retail concessions located in airports and travel plazas across the United States. Operating nearly 400 locations across 27 airports and 12 travel plazas nationwide, the company is one of the largest privately held travel hospitality operators in the United States and the U.S. division of Areas, a global leader in travel hospitality. The COO partners with the CEO and executive team to set strategic direction, drives consistent operational excellence across all regions and concepts, and serves as the company's primary executive liaison to airport authorities, travel plaza landlords, and national brand partners. This role is accountable for building and leading a high\-performing multi\-unit operations organization that delivers a strong operating culture, brand standards, safety, and profitability across a large, geographically dispersed portfolio. A modern, hands\-on COO in this role is closely engaged in day\-to\-day execution, builds a strong culture of accountability and continuous improvement across the organization, drives operational effectiveness and data\-driven decision\-making, champions sustainability and diversity and inclusion initiatives (including the company's Airport Concession Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (ACDBE) commitments), and partners with Areas' global leadership team to share best practices and support the U.S. division's continued growth through organic expansion and acquisition integration.

**Main Duties and Responsibilities:**

new_jobs.title: IAC Director of Development, Tri State Region
new_jobs.description:
**About the Israeli\-American Council (IAC)**


The mission of the IAC is to build an engaged and united Israeli\-American community that strengthens the Israeli and Jewish identity of the next generations, the American Jewish community, and the bond between the peoples of the United States and the State of Israel.

 **Position Overview**

  

The **Director of Development** is a senior fundraising professional responsible for leading all philanthropic activities within an assigned region. This individual develops and executes a comprehensive regional fundraising strategy, manages a portfolio of major donors and prospects, and works closely with Regional Directors, volunteer leadership, and the national Development team to achieve ambitious fundraising goals. The Director of Development serves as a strategic partner to regional leadership and acts as a trusted advisor to donors, helping them align their philanthropic interests with the IAC’s mission and priorities. This is an entrepreneurial, externally facing role requiring exceptional relationship\-building skills, strategic thinking, and a demonstrated ability to secure transformational philanthropic investments. The Director of Development reports to the **Chief Communities \& Growth Officer** and works closely with Regional Directors and senior organizational leadership.

 **Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:** **Regional Fundraising Strategy**

* Develop and implement the annual regional development plan aligned with the IAC’s national fundraising priorities.
* Identify new philanthropic opportunities and expand the regional donor pipeline.
* Analyze fundraising performance and adjust strategies to maximize results.
* Create annual revenue forecasts and monitor progress toward goals.

 **Major Gifts \& Donor Portfolio Management**

* Manage a portfolio of major donors and high\-capacity prospects through all stages of moves management, including identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and renewal.
* Develop and execute individualized strategies to secure five\-, six\-, and seven\-figure gifts.
* Meet or exceed annual fundraising goals and key performance indicators.
* Build long\-term relationships with philanthropists, family foundations, corporations, donor\-advised funds, and community leaders.
* Prepare compelling proposals, gift agreements, stewardship reports, and impact communications.

 **Donor Engagement \& Stewardship**

* Design and execute meaningful donor stewardship plans that strengthen engagement and inspire increased giving.
* Partner with senior leadership to cultivate strategic donor relationships.
* Represent the IAC at donor meetings, community gatherings, and regional events.
* Serve as a passionate ambassador for the organization’s mission and impact.

 **Events \& Community Engagement**

* Lead fundraising strategy for regional galas, leadership receptions, parlor meetings, donor briefings, and mission\-related events.
* Collaborate with Regional Directors and volunteer leadership to maximize sponsorships, ticket sales, and philanthropic giving.
* Leverage events as opportunities to cultivate new donors and deepen existing relationships.

 **Development Operations**

* Maintain accurate donor records, moves management activities, and revenue forecasts in the organization’s CRM.
* Utilize data and analytics to guide fundraising strategy and portfolio management.
* Prepare reports, dashboards, and pipeline updates for senior leadership.

 **Skills/Qualifications**  

* Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree or CFRE certification preferred.
* Minimum of **7 years of progressively responsible fundraising experience**, including major gifts.
* Demonstrated success securing and closing five\-, six\-, and preferably seven\-figure philanthropic gifts.
* Proven experience managing complex donor portfolios \& sophisticated moves management strategies.
* Strong understanding of principal gifts, annual giving, corporate partnerships, foundations, and planned giving opportunities.
* Exceptional interpersonal, communication, presentation, and negotiation skills.
* Experience working with high\-net\-worth individuals, volunteer leadership, and governing boards.
* Entrepreneurial mindset with outstanding organizational and project management skills.
* Highly self\-motivated with the ability to work independently while collaborating across departments.
* Advanced proficiency with CRM systems and fundraising analytics.
* Knowledge of the Israeli American and broader Jewish philanthropic community strongly preferred.
* Fluent English required; conversational Hebrew strongly preferred.
* Willingness to work evenings, weekends, and travel throughout the assigned region and nationally as needed.

 **Key Performance Indicators**


Success in this role will be measured by:

* Achievement of annual and quarterly fundraising revenue goals.
* Growth in major gift revenue.
* Expansion of the regional donor pipeline.
* Increased donor retention and donor upgrades.
* Successful acquisition of new major donors.
* Execution of high\-impact fundraising events.
* Accurate CRM management, reporting, and forecasting.
* Strengthened engagement of volunteer leadership and strategic partners.

 **Compensation \& Benefits**


The Israeli\-American Council offers a competitive compensation package, comprehensive health benefits, retirement plan, generous paid time off, professional development opportunities, and the chance to be part of one of North America’s fastest\-growing Jewish nonprofit organizations.


Salary is commensurate with experience and geographic market.

 **Why Join the IAC?**


Joining the IAC means becoming part of a mission\-driven organization that is shaping the future of the Israeli\-American and Jewish communities. You will work alongside passionate colleagues, visionary philanthropists, and community leaders to strengthen Jewish identity, inspire civic engagement, support I
